writing.tips: Net bir tez cümlesiyle başla. Görüşünü iki ya da üç gerekçe ve örnekle destekle, karşı görüşe kısaca değin ve tezini yineleyerek kapat. Bağlaçları doğru kullan (however, for example).
writing.structure: Tez -> gerekçe 1 + örnek -> gerekçe 2 + örnek -> karşı görüşe kısa değini -> sonuç.

writing.prompt: Describe your favourite place in your town or city. Explain what it looks like and why you like it.
writing.tips: Yeri tanıt, duyulara hitap eden sıfatlar kullan (busy, quiet, colourful), neden sevdiğini açıkla ve kısa kişisel bir anıyla renklendir.
writing.structure: Yerin tanıtımı -> görünümün betimi -> neden sevdiğin -> kişisel anı + kapanış.

writing.prompt: Some people believe that modern technology is making people less creative. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
writing.tips: Giriş'te konuyu kendi sözcüklerinle yeniden ifade et ve net bir duruş belirt. Her gövde paragrafı tek bir ana fikir, açıklama ve örnek içersin. Akademik bağlaçlar kullan (furthermore, however) ve sonuçta görüşünü özetle.
writing.structure: Giriş (parafraz + tez) -> gövde 1 (fikir + örnek) -> gövde 2 (fikir + örnek) -> sonuç.

writing.prompt: The chart below shows the number of international tourists visiting three cities between 2010 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
writing.tips: Giriş'te grafiği kendi cümlenle tanıt. En belirgin eğilimleri (overview) bir-iki cümlede özetle. Sayıları ve eğilim fiillerini kullan (rose, fell, peaked, remained stable). Görüş ekleme; yalnızca betimle ve karşılaştır.
writing.structure: Giriş (grafiğin tanıtımı) -> genel eğilim (overview) -> ayrıntı 1 -> ayrıntı 2 + karşılaştırmalar.

writing.prompt: Some people think universities should focus on practical job skills, while others believe their main role is to develop broad academic knowledge. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
writing.tips: Her iki görüşü de ayrı paragraflarda adil biçimde sun. Kendi görüşünü açıkça belirt ve girişle sonuç arasında tutarlı tut. Her noktayı örnekle destekle ve dengeli, akademik bir ton koru.
writing.structure: Giriş (parafraz + tez) -> 1. görüş -> 2. görüş -> kendi görüşün -> sonuç.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the following statement? 'It is better to work for a large company than for a small one.' Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer.
writing.tips: Net bir duruşla başla. İki ya da üç güçlü gerekçeyi ayrı paragraflarda örneklerle geliştir; kişisel deneyim örnekleri kabul edilir. Sonuç paragrafında tezini yinele.
writing.structure: Giriş (tez) -> gerekçe 1 + örnek -> gerekçe 2 + örnek -> sonuç.

writing.prompt: You will read a short passage and then hear a lecture on the same topic. Summarise the points made in the lecture, explaining how they cast doubt on the points made in the reading.
writing.tips: Kendi fikrini ekleme; yalnızca okuma ve dinlemeyi özetle ve karşılaştır. Dinlemenin okumadaki her noktayı nasıl çürüttüğünü açıkla. Aktarım kalıpları kullan (The lecturer argues..., whereas the reading claims...).
writing.structure: Giriş (genel ilişki) -> nokta 1 (okuma vs dinleme) -> nokta 2 -> nokta 3.

writing.prompt: Governments should ban single-use plastics in order to protect the environment. To what extent do you agree? Support your position with reasons and examples.
writing.tips: Açık bir tez belirle. Güçlü argümanlarını kanıt ve örneklerle destekle, en az bir karşı argümana yanıt vererek çürüt. Resmî, tutarlı ve akademik bir ton kullan; sonuçta bir öneri ya da çağrıyla kapat.
writing.structure: Giriş (tez) -> argüman 1 + kanıt -> argüman 2 + kanıt -> karşı argüman + çürütme -> sonuç.

writing.prompt: A friend helped you move into your new flat last weekend. Write a short email to thank them and invite them for dinner.
writing.tips: Samimi bir selamlamayla başla (Hi / Dear). Tam olarak ne için teşekkür ettiğini belirt, yardımın sana nasıl iyi geldiğini söyle, küçük bir karşılık (akşam yemeği daveti) sun ve sıcak bir kapanış yaz.
writing.structure: Selamlama -> teşekkür + neden -> kısa duygu/yorum -> davet -> sıcak kapanış.

writing.prompt: You missed your friend's birthday party. Write a letter to apologise, explain why you could not come, and suggest meeting soon.
writing.tips: Özrünü açıkça ve içtenlikle ifade et (I'm really sorry ...). Gelememe nedenini kısaca açıkla, üzüldüğünü belirt ve telafi için somut bir öneri (buluşma) sun. Nazik bir kapanışla bitir.
writing.structure: Selamlama -> özür -> açıklama (neden) -> üzüntü ifadesi -> telafi önerisi -> kapanış.

writing.prompt: Your class is organising a charity book sale at school. Write a short announcement to inform other students about it.
writing.tips: Net bir başlıkla başla. Etkinliğin ne olduğunu, tarihini, yerini ve saatini açıkça yaz. İnsanları neden katılmaya çağırdığını belirt (iyi bir amaç). Kısa, açık ve davetkâr bir dil kullan.
writing.structure: Başlık -> etkinlik nedir -> tarih/yer/saat -> neden katılmalı -> kapanış çağrısı.

writing.prompt: A friend from abroad is going to visit your city for three days and asks what to do. Write an email giving advice.
writing.tips: Selamlamadan sonra arkadaşını mutlu et (I'm so excited ...). Görülecek iki-üç yer öner, neden tavsiye ettiğini kısaca açıkla, pratik bir ipucu (hava, ulaşım) ekle ve görüşmeyi dört gözle beklediğini söyle.
writing.structure: Selamlama -> heyecan ifadesi -> öneri 1-2-3 + kısa neden -> pratik ipucu -> sıcak kapanış.

writing.prompt: Write a blog post about a hobby that has changed your life, explaining what it is and why you recommend it to others.
writing.tips: Okuru çeken bir girişle başla. Hobiyi tanıt, sana neler kattığını somut örneklerle anlat, başkalarının da neden denemesi gerektiğini söyle. Samimi ama düzenli bir ton kullan; okuyucuya doğrudan seslen.
writing.structure: İlgi çekici giriş -> hobi nedir -> sana etkisi + örnek -> okuyucuya öneri -> kapanış sorusu/çağrısı.

writing.prompt: More and more people are working from home rather than in an office. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
writing.tips: Giriş'te konuyu parafraz et ve duruşunu belirt. Bir gövde paragrafında avantajları, diğerinde dezavantajları örneklerle sun. Sonuçta hangisinin ağır bastığına dair net bir yargı ver. Akademik bağlaçlar (on the one hand, however) kullan.
writing.structure: Giriş (parafraz + tez) -> avantajlar + örnek -> dezavantajlar + örnek -> tartılı sonuç.

writing.prompt: The diagram below shows how paper is recycled. Summarise the information by describing the main stages of the process.
writing.tips: Giriş'te süreci kendi cümlenle tanıt ve kaç aşamadan oluştuğunu söyle. Aşamaları sırayla ve edilgen yapıyla anlat (is collected, is cleaned). Sıra bağlaçları kullan (first, then, after that, finally). Görüş ekleme; yalnızca betimle.
writing.structure: Giriş (sürecin tanıtımı) -> genel bakış (kaç aşama) -> aşamalar sırayla -> son ürün/kapanış.

writing.prompt: Your manager has asked you to assess the staff canteen and suggest improvements. Write a formal report with findings and recommendations.
writing.tips: Başlık ve kısa bir amaç cümlesiyle başla. Bulguları başlıklar altında nesnel biçimde sun (yemek kalitesi, fiyat, ortam). Her bulguyu somut gözleme dayandır ve net, uygulanabilir öneriler ver. Resmî, kişisellikten uzak bir dil kullan.
writing.structure: Başlık + amaç -> bulgular (alt başlıklarla) -> değerlendirme -> öneriler -> kısa kapanış.

writing.prompt: Traffic congestion is becoming a serious problem in many large cities. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
writing.tips: Giriş'te sorunu parafraz et ve denemenin yapısını ima et. Bir gövde paragrafında nedenleri, diğerinde çözümleri ele al; her çözümü olası sonucuyla birlikte açıkla. Sonuçta en etkili çözümü vurgula. Resmî ve tutarlı bir ton koru.
writing.structure: Giriş (parafraz) -> nedenler + açıklama -> çözümler + olası sonuç -> sonuç.

writing.prompt: Some people prefer to plan their activities for their free time very carefully. Others choose not to make any plans at all. Which do you prefer, and why?
writing.tips: Net bir tercih belirterek başla. İki-üç güçlü gerekçeyi ayrı paragraflarda örneklerle geliştir; kişisel deneyim örnekleri kabul edilir. Karşı tercihi kısaca kabul edip neden seninkini yeğlediğini açıkla. Sonuçta tercihini yinele.
writing.structure: Giriş (tercih) -> gerekçe 1 + örnek -> gerekçe 2 + örnek -> karşı tercihe kısa değini -> sonuç.

cloze.title: Ottoman Overland Trade
cloze.text: For several centuries the Ottoman Empire occupied a strategic position between Europe and Asia, and this geography (1) ____ much of its early economic policy. Control of the principal overland routes allowed the state to (2) ____ substantial revenues by taxing the caravans that crossed its territory. As European powers established direct maritime routes to Asia, however, the volume of goods passing through Ottoman lands gradually (3) ____, and customs income fell accordingly. Confronted with this decline, the administration attempted to (4) ____ alternative sources of wealth, encouraging domestic manufacture and reforming the system of taxation. These measures, though partially effective, could not entirely (5) ____ the long-term redirection of global commerce towards the oceans, a shift that ultimately reshaped the empire's place in the world economy.

blanks.tr: 'shaped much of its policy' = politikasının çoğunu biçimlendirdi; coğrafya ekonomik politikayı belirleyen özne olduğu için 'shaped' doğru. 'concealed/neglected' bağlamla çelişir.
blanks.en: 'shaped much of its policy' fits: geography determined economic policy. 'concealed/neglected' contradict the context.

blanks.tr: 'extract revenues by taxing' = vergilendirerek gelir elde etmek; vergiden gelir 'çekip çıkarılır'. 'waive/forgive' (vazgeçmek/bağışlamak) anlamı tersine çevirir.
blanks.en: 'extract revenues by taxing' is right: revenue is drawn from taxes. 'waive/forgive' reverse the meaning.

blanks.tr: Deniz yolları açılınca karadan geçen mal hacmi 'diminished' (azaldı); ardından gelen 'customs income fell' ifadesi bunu doğrular. 'expanded/doubled' artış demek olup çelişir.
blanks.en: With sea routes opening, overland volume 'diminished'; 'customs income fell' confirms it. 'expanded/doubled' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'develop alternative sources of wealth' = alternatif zenginlik kaynakları geliştirmek; sonraki 'encouraging manufacture' bunu örnekler. 'abandon/overlook' niyetle çelişir.
blanks.en: 'develop alternative sources of wealth' fits; 'encouraging manufacture' illustrates it. 'abandon/overlook' contradict the intent.

blanks.tr: 'offset the redirection' = yön değişiminin etkisini dengelemek/telafi etmek; önlemler kısmen etkili ama kaymayı tam telafi edemedi. 'accelerate' tersini söyler.
blanks.en: 'offset the redirection' = counterbalance the shift; measures could not fully compensate. 'accelerate' says the opposite.

cloze.title: Coral Reef Decline
cloze.text: Coral reefs support a remarkable proportion of marine biodiversity, yet they are extraordinarily (1) ____ to even small changes in their environment. When sea temperatures rise beyond a narrow tolerance, corals expel the symbiotic algae on which they (2) ____ for most of their energy, losing their colour in a process known as bleaching. If warm conditions (3) ____ for long enough, the weakened corals die and the intricate structures they have built over centuries begin to collapse. Scientists warn that the frequency of such events has increased markedly, leaving reefs with insufficient time to (4) ____ between successive shocks. Although some species show signs of greater heat resistance, researchers caution that adaptation alone is unlikely to (5) ____ the scale of warming now projected for the coming decades.

blanks.tr: 'vulnerable to changes' = değişimlere karşı kırılgan; küçük çevresel değişimden zarar gören mercanlar için doğru. 'indifferent' (kayıtsız) anlamla çelişir.
blanks.en: 'vulnerable to changes' is correct: reefs are harmed by small shifts. 'indifferent' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'rely on ... for energy' = enerji için ona bağımlı olmak; mercan enerjisini alglerden alır. 'rely on' kalıbı 'for' ile gelir.
blanks.en: 'rely on ... for energy' fits: corals depend on algae. The collocation 'rely on' pairs with 'for'.

blanks.tr: 'if warm conditions persist' = sıcak koşullar yeterince sürerse; sonrasındaki ölüm bunun sonucudur. 'vanish/cool' koşulu ortadan kaldırır.
blanks.en: 'if warm conditions persist' fits; death follows from prolonged heat. 'vanish/cool' remove the condition.

blanks.tr: 'time to recover between shocks' = şoklar arasında toparlanacak zaman; sık olaylar toparlanmayı engeller. Diğer fiiller bağlamı tam karşılamaz.
blanks.en: 'time to recover between shocks' is right: frequent events prevent recovery. The other verbs don't fit the gap.

blanks.tr: 'adaptation is unlikely to match the scale of warming' = uyum, ısınmanın ölçüsüne yetişemez; 'match' burada 'denk gelmek/yetişmek' anlamında. 'cause/predict' mantıksız.
blanks.en: 'unlikely to match the scale of warming' = adaptation cannot keep pace. 'cause/predict' are illogical here.

cloze.title: Sleep and Memory
cloze.text: The idea that sleep merely allows the body to rest has been steadily revised as researchers have come to (1) ____ its active role in learning. During the night the brain does not simply switch off; instead it (2) ____ the experiences of the previous day, strengthening certain neural connections while weakening others. This selective process appears to be essential for converting fragile, short-term traces into more (3) ____ long-term memories. Experiments in which volunteers are deprived of sleep consistently show (4) ____ performance on tasks that depend on recall, even when the participants believe they have compensated for their tiredness. Such findings have led many specialists to argue that adequate sleep should be regarded not as a luxury but as a (5) ____ component of effective study and sound mental health.

blanks.tr: 'come to appreciate its active role' = etkin rolünü takdir etmeye/anlamaya başlamak; eski görüşün revize edildiği bağlamla uyumlu. 'deny/doubt' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'come to appreciate its active role' fits the revised view. 'deny/doubt' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'processes the experiences' = deneyimleri işler; sonraki 'strengthening connections' bunu açıklar. 'erases/invents' bağlama aykırı.
blanks.en: 'processes the experiences' is right; 'strengthening connections' explains it. 'erases/invents' don't fit.

blanks.tr: 'more durable long-term memories' = daha kalıcı uzun süreli anılar; kısa süreliyle karşıtlık kurulur. 'temporary' tam tersidir.
blanks.en: 'more durable long-term memories' contrasts with short-term traces. 'temporary' is the opposite.

blanks.tr: 'impaired performance' = bozulmuş performans; uyku yoksunluğunun beklenen sonucu. 'improved/flawless' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'impaired performance' is the expected result of sleep deprivation. 'improved/flawless' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'a necessary component' = gerekli bir bileşen; 'not a luxury but' yapısı zorunluluğa işaret eder. 'trivial/optional' bu karşıtlıkla uyumsuz.
blanks.en: 'a necessary component' fits the 'not a luxury but' structure. 'trivial/optional' clash with that contrast.

cloze.title: Central Banks and Inflation
cloze.text: Modern central banks are widely expected to keep inflation low and (1) ____, a task that is far more delicate than it may first appear. When prices rise too quickly, the purchasing power of households (2) ____, and savings lose their value, undermining confidence in the currency. To counter this, banks often raise interest rates, which tends to (3) ____ borrowing and spending throughout the economy. Yet the same instrument carries clear risks: if rates are pushed too high, economic activity may slow so sharply that unemployment (4) ____. Policymakers must therefore weigh competing dangers, and they rely heavily on forecasts that are inevitably (5) ____, since the future behaviour of consumers and firms can never be known with certainty.

blanks.tr: 'low and stable' = düşük ve istikrarlı; enflasyon hedefinin standart ifadesi. 'volatile' (oynak) hedefle çelişir.
blanks.en: 'low and stable' is the standard inflation target phrasing. 'volatile' contradicts the goal.

blanks.tr: 'purchasing power erodes' = alım gücü aşınır; hızlı fiyat artışının sonucu. 'rises/doubles' tersini söyler.
blanks.en: 'purchasing power erodes' results from fast price rises. 'rises/doubles' say the opposite.

blanks.tr: Faiz artışı borçlanma ve harcamayı 'restrain' eder (kısıtlar). 'encourage' faiz artışının etkisiyle çelişir.
blanks.en: Higher rates 'restrain' borrowing and spending. 'encourage' contradicts the effect of rate rises.

blanks.tr: Aşırı yavaşlamada işsizlik 'rises' (artar). Bağlam 'risks' ve 'too high' ile olumsuz sonuca işaret eder.
blanks.en: If activity slows sharply, unemployment 'rises'. The context of risks points to a negative outcome.

blanks.tr: 'inevitably imprecise' = kaçınılmaz olarak belirsiz/kesin olmayan; geleceğin bilinememesiyle uyumlu. 'certain/final' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'inevitably imprecise' matches the uncertainty of the future. 'certain/final' contradict.

cloze.title: The First Settlements
cloze.text: The shift from a mobile, hunting way of life to permanent settlement was one of the most (1) ____ transformations in human history. As communities began to cultivate crops, they could no longer move freely in search of food and were obliged to (2) ____ near their fields. This new permanence encouraged the construction of durable houses, the storage of surplus grain, and, in time, the emergence of more complex social arrangements. Archaeologists who excavate such sites must interpret fragmentary evidence with great care, for a single layer of soil may (3) ____ centuries of occupation. By comparing the remains of tools, seeds, and dwellings, they attempt to (4) ____ how daily life was organised long before the invention of writing. Their conclusions, though necessarily (5) ____, have transformed our understanding of how civilisation began.

blanks.tr: 'profound transformations' = köklü/derin dönüşümler; insanlık tarihinin en önemli değişimi vurgusuyla uyumlu. 'trivial' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'profound transformations' fits the emphasis on a major change. 'trivial' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'obliged to settle near their fields' = tarlalarının yakınına yerleşmek zorunda; yerleşik yaşam bağlamı. 'wander' (dolaşmak) tersidir.
blanks.en: 'obliged to settle near their fields' fits sedentism. 'wander' is the opposite.

blanks.tr: 'a single layer may represent centuries' = tek bir tabaka yüzyılları temsil edebilir; arkeolojik yorumlama güçlüğünü anlatır. 'erase' mantıksız.
blanks.en: 'a single layer may represent centuries' explains the interpretive difficulty. 'erase' is illogical.

blanks.tr: 'reconstruct how daily life was organised' = günlük yaşamın nasıl düzenlendiğini yeniden kurmak; arkeologların amacı. Diğerleri bağlama aykırı.
blanks.en: 'reconstruct how daily life was organised' is the archaeologists' aim. The others contradict the context.

blanks.tr: 'necessarily tentative' = ister istemez geçici/ihtiyatlı; parçalı kanıttan çıkarılan sonuçlar kesin değildir. 'permanent' uymaz.
blanks.en: 'necessarily tentative' fits conclusions drawn from fragmentary evidence. 'permanent' doesn't fit.

cloze.title: Renewable Energy and the Grid
cloze.text: As countries try to reduce their dependence on fossil fuels, they are installing more wind turbines and solar panels than ever before. These sources are clean, but they are also (1) ____, because the wind does not always blow and the sun does not always shine. To keep the electricity supply (2) ____, engineers must find ways to store energy when production is high and release it when demand increases. Large batteries can help, yet they remain expensive and cannot yet (3) ____ the needs of an entire nation. Another approach is to connect distant regions, so that a shortage in one area can be (4) ____ by a surplus in another. Together, these strategies are gradually making renewable power a more (5) ____ part of the modern energy system.

blanks.tr: 'intermittent' = kesintili; rüzgârın ve güneşin sürekli olmadığı açıklamasıyla uyumlu. 'reliable' tersidir.
blanks.en: 'intermittent' matches the note that wind/sun are not constant. 'reliable' is the opposite.

blanks.tr: 'keep the supply steady' = arzı istikrarlı tutmak; depolama amacının nedeni. 'unstable' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'keep the supply steady' is the goal of storage. 'unstable' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'meet the needs' = ihtiyaçları karşılamak; bataryaların henüz ülke çapında ihtiyacı karşılayamadığını söyler. 'meet the needs' yerleşik kalıptır.
blanks.en: 'meet the needs' is the set phrase: batteries can't yet supply a whole nation.

blanks.tr: 'offset by a surplus' = bir bölgedeki açık başka bölgedeki fazlayla dengelenir. 'caused' mantığı bozar.
blanks.en: 'offset by a surplus' = a shortage balanced by surplus elsewhere. 'caused' breaks the logic.

blanks.tr: 'a more dependable part' = daha güvenilir bir parça; stratejilerin amacı yenilenebiliri güvenilir kılmaktır. 'minor' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'a more dependable part' is the aim of the strategies. 'minor' contradicts.

cloze.title: A Short History of Vaccines
cloze.text: The principle behind vaccination is surprisingly simple: the body is shown a harmless version of a germ so that it can learn to (1) ____ the real threat later. Before this idea was understood, diseases that are now rare killed enormous numbers of people every year. Early experiments were often risky, and many doctors were (2) ____ to accept methods they could not fully explain. Over time, however, careful observation showed that vaccinated people were far less likely to (3) ____ certain illnesses. As laboratories improved, scientists were able to produce vaccines that were both safer and more (4) ____, protecting whole communities rather than single individuals. Today, widespread vaccination is regarded as one of the most (5) ____ achievements of modern medicine, even though debates about it still appear from time to time.

blanks.tr: 'learn to recognise the real threat' = gerçek tehdidi tanımayı öğrenmek; bağışıklığın çalışma biçimi. 'ignore/spread' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'learn to recognise the real threat' explains how immunity works. 'ignore/spread' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'reluctant to accept' = kabul etmekte isteksiz; açıklanamayan yönteme karşı doktorların tutumu. 'eager' tersidir.
blanks.en: 'reluctant to accept' fits doctors' attitude to an unexplained method. 'eager' is the opposite.

blanks.tr: 'less likely to catch certain illnesses' = belli hastalıkları kapma olasılığı daha düşük; aşının koruyucu etkisi. 'cure/prevent' özneyle uyumsuz.
blanks.en: 'less likely to catch certain illnesses' fits the protective effect. 'cure/prevent' don't match the subject.

blanks.tr: 'safer and more effective' = daha güvenli ve daha etkili; bilimsel ilerlemenin sonucu. 'fragile/rare' bağlama aykırı.
blanks.en: 'safer and more effective' fits scientific progress. 'fragile/rare' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'one of the most important achievements' = en önemli başarılardan biri; tıp tarihindeki yeri. 'doubtful/forgotten' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'one of the most important achievements' fits its place in medicine. 'doubtful/forgotten' contradict.

cloze.title: Social Media and Attention
cloze.text: Social media platforms are designed to hold our attention for as long as possible, and they are remarkably (1) ____ at doing so. Every notification, every new post, and every brief video is carefully arranged to keep us (2) ____ in the screen. Researchers have begun to ask what effect this constant stimulation has on our ability to (3) ____ on a single task. Some studies suggest that frequent switching between apps may make it harder to read a long text or follow a complex argument without becoming (4) ____. Critics therefore argue that users should learn to set clear limits, turning off alerts and choosing deliberately when to log on. Used with awareness, these tools can be genuinely useful; used without it, they can quietly (5) ____ the very focus that serious work requires.

blanks.tr: 'remarkably successful at doing so' = bunu yapmakta dikkat çekici biçimde başarılı; dikkati tutma amacıyla uyumlu. 'poor' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'remarkably successful at doing so' fits the goal of holding attention. 'poor' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'keep us absorbed in the screen' = bizi ekrana dalmış tutmak; tasarımın hedefi. 'bored/absent' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'keep us absorbed in the screen' fits the design goal. 'bored/absent' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'concentrate on a single task' = tek bir göreve odaklanmak; 'on' edatıyla gelen kalıp. 'rely on' anlamı bozar.
blanks.en: 'concentrate on a single task' is the right collocation with 'on'. 'rely on' breaks the meaning.

blanks.tr: 'without becoming distracted' = dikkati dağılmadan; sık uygulama değiştirmenin olumsuz etkisi. 'interested/relaxed' uymaz.
blanks.en: 'without becoming distracted' fits the negative effect of app-switching. 'interested/relaxed' don't fit.

blanks.tr: 'quietly undermine the very focus' = ihtiyaç duyulan odağı sessizce baltalamak; 'without it' (farkındalık olmadan) olumsuz sonuç. 'sharpen' tersidir.
blanks.en: 'quietly undermine the very focus' fits the negative outcome 'without it'. 'sharpen' is the opposite.

cloze.title: Antibiotic Resistance
cloze.text: Antibiotics transformed medicine by making once-fatal infections routinely treatable, but their very success has created a serious new problem. Each time these drugs are used, the bacteria they target are placed under pressure, and the few that happen to (1) ____ the treatment survive to reproduce. Over many generations, this process allows resistant strains to become increasingly (2) ____, until some infections no longer respond to the medicines that once defeated them. The danger is made worse by the (3) ____ use of antibiotics in cases where they offer no benefit, such as ordinary viral colds. Health authorities are therefore urging both doctors and patients to use these drugs more (4) ____, reserving them for situations in which they are genuinely needed. Without such restraint, experts warn, we risk returning to an era in which a minor wound could once again prove (5) ____.

blanks.tr: 'withstand the treatment' = tedaviye dayanmak/karşı koymak; hayatta kalan dirençli bakteriler. 'request/enjoy' mantıksız.
blanks.en: 'withstand the treatment' fits surviving resistant bacteria. 'request/enjoy' are illogical.

blanks.tr: 'increasingly common' = giderek yaygınlaşan; dirençli suşların çoğalması. 'rare' süreçle çelişir.
blanks.en: 'increasingly common' fits resistant strains spreading. 'rare' contradicts the process.

blanks.tr: 'the unnecessary use' = gereksiz kullanım; viral soğuk algınlığı örneğiyle uyumlu. 'careful' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'the unnecessary use' fits the example of viral colds. 'careful' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'use these drugs more sparingly' = ilaçları daha tutumlu/idareli kullanmak; gerçekten gerekli durumlara saklamakla uyumlu. 'frequently' tersidir.
blanks.en: 'use these drugs more sparingly' fits reserving them for real need. 'frequently' is the opposite.

blanks.tr: 'a minor wound could prove fatal' = küçük bir yara ölümcül olabilir; antibiyotik öncesi döneme dönüş uyarısı. 'harmless' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'a minor wound could prove fatal' fits the warning of a pre-antibiotic era. 'harmless' contradicts.

cloze.title: The Urban Heat Island
cloze.text: Anyone who has walked through a city on a hot summer evening will have noticed that it feels warmer than the countryside nearby. This difference is not imagined; it is a well-documented effect that scientists (1) ____ the urban heat island. Concrete, asphalt, and brick absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night, so the air in dense neighbourhoods stays warm long after the surrounding fields have begun to (2) ____. The problem is made worse by the lack of trees, whose shade and moisture would otherwise help to (3) ____ the temperature. As summers become hotter, this extra warmth can pose a real (4) ____ to elderly residents and to people who are already unwell. Planners are therefore looking at simple measures, such as planting more greenery and using lighter materials, that could make crowded cities noticeably more (5) ____.

blanks.tr: 'scientists call the urban heat island' = bilim insanlarının kentsel ısı adası dediği; bir olguya isim verme. 'call' burada 'adlandırmak'.
blanks.en: 'scientists call the urban heat island' = name the phenomenon. 'call' here means 'name'.

blanks.tr: 'fields have begun to cool' = kırların serinlemeye başlaması; şehirle karşıtlık. 'warm' tersini söyler.
blanks.en: 'fields have begun to cool' contrasts with the warm city. 'warm' says the opposite.

blanks.tr: 'help to lower the temperature' = sıcaklığı düşürmeye yardımcı olmak; ağaç gölgesinin işlevi. 'raise' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'help to lower the temperature' fits the role of shade. 'raise' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'pose a real risk to elderly residents' = yaşlı sakinlere gerçek bir tehlike oluşturmak; aşırı sıcağın olumsuz etkisi. 'benefit' çelişir.
blanks.en: 'pose a real risk to elderly residents' fits the danger of extra heat. 'benefit' contradicts.

blanks.tr: 'noticeably more cooler' → doğru sözcük 'cooler'; önlemlerin amacı şehri serinletmek. 'hotter' amacı tersine çevirir.
blanks.en: 'noticeably cooler' fits: the measures aim to cool cities. 'hotter' reverses the aim.

cloze.title: The Shape of Life
cloze.text: The discovery of the structure of DNA is often described as one of the most important moments in the history of biology. For years, scientists knew that this molecule somehow (1) ____ the instructions that living things pass to their offspring, but its exact form remained a mystery. When researchers finally showed that DNA takes the shape of a twisted ladder, the elegance of the design immediately (2) ____ how copying might occur. Each side of the ladder could serve as a template from which a new, identical partner was (3) ____. This insight transformed the field, for it explained how information could be (4) ____ faithfully from one generation to the next. Later work revealed that small changes, or mutations, in the sequence can (5) ____ the way an organism develops, providing the raw material on which evolution acts.

blanks.tr: 'carried the instructions' = talimatları taşıyordu; DNA kalıtsal bilgiyi taşır. 'hid/ignored' bağlama aykırı.
blanks.en: 'carried the instructions' fits: DNA holds hereditary information. 'hid/ignored' contradict.

blanks.tr: 'suggested how copying might occur' = kopyalamanın nasıl olabileceğini düşündürdü; tasarımın zarafeti mekanizmayı ima eder.
blanks.en: 'suggested how copying might occur' fits: the design hinted at the mechanism.

blanks.tr: 'a new partner was built' = yeni bir eş inşa edildi; şablondan yeni zincir oluşturulur.
blanks.en: 'a new partner was built' fits: a new strand is formed from the template.

blanks.tr: 'information could be copied faithfully' = bilgi sadakatle kopyalanabilir; kalıtımın özü.
blanks.en: 'information could be copied faithfully' captures inheritance.

blanks.tr: 'mutations can alter the way an organism develops' = mutasyonlar gelişimi değiştirebilir; evrimin ham maddesi.
blanks.en: 'mutations can alter development' provides the raw material for evolution.

cloze.title: Art and Its Patrons
cloze.text: The extraordinary flowering of painting and sculpture during the Renaissance cannot be understood without considering the people who paid for it. Wealthy merchants and powerful families competed to (1) ____ the finest artists, treating great works as a sign of their own taste and status. Far from being free to follow their own vision, painters often had to (2) ____ the detailed wishes of those who commissioned them, from the subject of a picture to the precise colours used. Yet this system did not (3) ____ creativity; on the contrary, the steady supply of money allowed artists to experiment with new techniques and materials. Over time, the most successful masters gained enough reputation to (4) ____ greater independence, choosing their own subjects and charging high fees. The relationship between art and wealth, then, was far more (5) ____ than the popular image of the lonely genius suggests.

blanks.tr: 'employ the finest artists' = en iyi sanatçıları çalıştırmak; hamiler usta peşindeydi.
blanks.en: 'employ the finest artists' fits patrons competing for talent.

blanks.tr: 'follow the detailed wishes' = ayrıntılı istekleri izlemek; sipariş veren belirlerdi.
blanks.en: 'follow the detailed wishes' fits: commissioners dictated terms.

blanks.tr: 'did not crush creativity' = yaratıcılığı ezmedi; sonraki 'on the contrary' karşıtlık kurar.
blanks.en: 'did not crush creativity' fits the 'on the contrary' that follows.

blanks.tr: 'win greater independence' = daha fazla bağımsızlık kazanmak; ün bağımsızlık getirdi.
blanks.en: 'win greater independence' fits: reputation brought freedom.

blanks.tr: 'far more complex' = çok daha karmaşık; yalnız dâhi imgesiyle çelişir.
blanks.en: 'far more complex' contrasts with the lonely-genius image.

cloze.title: The Bacteria Within
cloze.text: For most of medical history, the bacteria living inside the human body were seen mainly as a source of disease. Recently, however, scientists have begun to (1) ____ that many of these tiny organisms are in fact helpful. The community of microbes in our intestines, sometimes called the gut flora, helps us to (2) ____ food that we could not break down on our own. These bacteria also produce certain vitamins and appear to (3) ____ the immune system, teaching it to tell friend from enemy. When the balance of this community is (4) ____, perhaps by a poor diet or a course of antibiotics, the effects can reach far beyond the stomach. Some studies even suggest a link to mood, which is why researchers are now so (5) ____ to understand how these invisible partners shape our health.

blanks.tr: 'realise that many are helpful' = çoğunun yararlı olduğunu fark etmek; eski görüşün revizyonu.
blanks.en: 'realise that many are helpful' fits the revised view.

blanks.tr: 'digest food' = yiyeceği sindirmek; bağırsak florasının işlevi.
blanks.en: 'digest food' is the gut flora's function.

blanks.tr: 'support the immune system' = bağışıklığı desteklemek; sonrasında 'teaching it' bunu açıklar.
blanks.en: 'support the immune system' fits 'teaching it to tell friend from enemy'.

blanks.tr: 'the balance is disturbed' = denge bozulduğunda; kötü diyet/antibiyotik örneği.
blanks.en: 'the balance is disturbed' fits the diet/antibiotic example.

blanks.tr: 'so keen to understand' = anlamaya öyle istekli; araştırma ilgisinin nedeni.
blanks.en: 'so keen to understand' fits researchers' interest.

cloze.title: When the Forests Fall
cloze.text: Tropical forests are sometimes called the lungs of the planet, yet vast areas of them are cleared every year. The most obvious reason is economic: land that (1) ____ trees can be sold or used to grow crops and raise cattle. The consequences, however, reach far beyond the cleared ground itself. Forests store enormous amounts of carbon, and when they are burned this carbon is (2) ____ into the atmosphere, adding to global warming. The loss of trees also (3) ____ countless species of their only habitat, driving some towards extinction. Perhaps less obviously, large forests help to (4) ____ rainfall across whole regions, so their removal can make distant farmland drier. For all these reasons, many governments and organisations are now searching for ways to make standing forests more (5) ____ than the land beneath them.

blanks.tr: 'land that once held trees' = bir zamanlar ağaç olan toprak; temizlenen arazi.
blanks.en: 'land that once held trees' describes cleared ground.

blanks.tr: 'carbon is released into the atmosphere' = karbon atmosfere salınır; yanma ile.
blanks.en: 'carbon is released' fits burning forests.

blanks.tr: 'deprives countless species of their habitat' = türleri yaşam alanından yoksun bırakır.
blanks.en: 'deprives species of their habitat' fits extinction risk.

blanks.tr: 'help to regulate rainfall' = yağışı düzenlemeye yardımcı olmak; ormanın bölgesel rolü.
blanks.en: 'help to regulate rainfall' fits forests' regional role.

blanks.tr: 'more valuable than the land beneath' = altındaki topraktan daha değerli; koruma teşviki.
blanks.en: 'more valuable than the land beneath' fits the conservation incentive.

cloze.title: The Limits of Rational Choice
cloze.text: Traditional economics long assumed that people make decisions in a coldly rational way, carefully weighing costs against benefits. In recent decades, however, a new field has (1) ____ this comfortable picture. By running careful experiments, researchers have shown that human choices are frequently (2) ____ by factors that have nothing to do with logic. The way a question is worded, the order in which options appear, or simply what other people are doing can all (3) ____ our decisions. We tend, for example, to fear a loss far more than we value an equal gain, a tendency that classical theory cannot easily (4) ____. Rather than dismissing such behaviour as mere error, the new approach treats it as a regular and predictable feature of the human mind, one that policymakers can take into account when they design (5) ____ that gently guide people towards better choices.

blanks.tr: 'challenged this comfortable picture' = bu rahat tabloyu sarstı; yeni alanın katkısı.
blanks.en: 'challenged this comfortable picture' fits the new field.

blanks.tr: 'choices are shaped by factors' = seçimler mantık dışı etkenlerce biçimlenir.
blanks.en: 'choices are shaped by factors' fits the finding.

blanks.tr: 'sway our decisions' = kararlarımızı etkilemek; bağlam etkisi.
blanks.en: 'sway our decisions' fits contextual influence.

blanks.tr: 'cannot easily explain' = kolayca açıklayamaz; klasik teorinin sınırı.
blanks.en: 'cannot easily explain' fits the limit of classical theory.

blanks.tr: 'design policies that gently guide' = nazikçe yönlendiren politikalar tasarlamak; dürtme teorisi.
blanks.en: 'policies that gently guide people' fits nudge-style design.

cloze.title: A Question of Supply
cloze.text: Organ transplantation is one of the great achievements of modern surgery, allowing a failing heart or kidney to be (1) ____ with a healthy one from a donor. The main obstacle is no longer the operation itself, which has become remarkably safe, but the chronic (2) ____ of suitable organs. Far more patients are waiting than there are donors available, and many die before a match can be (3) ____. To address this, some countries have changed their laws so that citizens are assumed to be donors unless they (4) ____ choose otherwise, a system that has raised donation rates. Scientists are also exploring bolder solutions, such as growing organs in the laboratory or adapting those of animals. Whatever the method, the goal is the same: to (5) ____ the painful gap between the number of organs needed and the number that can be found.

blanks.tr: 'replaced with a healthy one' = sağlıklısıyla değiştirilmek; nakil tanımı.
blanks.en: 'replaced with a healthy one' defines a transplant.

blanks.tr: 'chronic shortage of organs' = organ kıtlığı; ana sorun.
blanks.en: 'chronic shortage of organs' is the main obstacle.

blanks.tr: 'a match can be found' = uyumlu organ bulunabilir; bekleme listesi.
blanks.en: 'a match can be found' fits the waiting list.

blanks.tr: 'unless they actively choose otherwise' = aksini etkin biçimde seçmedikçe; varsayılan bağış.
blanks.en: 'actively choose otherwise' fits opt-out donation.

blanks.tr: 'close the painful gap' = acı veren açığı kapatmak; amaç.
blanks.en: 'close the gap' states the goal.

cloze.title: The Age of Machines
cloze.text: The Industrial Revolution changed human life more deeply than almost any event before it. Within a few generations, goods that had always been made slowly by hand began to be produced in vast (1) ____ by machines. People who had farmed the land for centuries moved into rapidly growing cities to (2) ____ work in the new factories. Life there was often hard: hours were long, wages were low, and the air was thick with smoke. Yet the changes also (3) ____ enormous wealth and, in time, cheaper goods for ordinary families. Perhaps most importantly, the period created a sense that the future need not (4) ____ the past, that human societies could be transformed by invention. The world we live in today, with its constant search for new technology, is in many ways the (5) ____ of those noisy early factories.

blanks.tr: 'produced in vast quantities' = büyük miktarlarda üretmek; makineyle seri üretim.
blanks.en: 'in vast quantities' fits machine production.

blanks.tr: 'to seek work in the factories' = fabrikada iş aramak; kente göç.
blanks.en: 'to seek work' fits migration to cities.

blanks.tr: 'created enormous wealth' = büyük servet yarattı; olumlu yön.
blanks.en: 'created enormous wealth' fits the positive side.

blanks.tr: 'need not resemble the past' = geçmişe benzemek zorunda değil; ilerleme fikri.
blanks.en: 'need not resemble the past' fits the idea of progress.

blanks.tr: 'the child of those early factories' = o erken fabrikaların çocuğu; süreklilik metaforu.
blanks.en: 'the child of those early factories' fits the continuity metaphor.

cloze.title: The Strange Rules of the Very Small
cloze.text: At the scale of atoms and the particles inside them, nature behaves in ways that seem to (1) ____ common sense. A particle that we might picture as a tiny ball can also act like a spreading wave, and until it is measured it appears to exist in several states at (2) ____. These ideas were so unfamiliar that even the scientists who developed them found the results difficult to (3) ____. Yet the theory has been tested countless times and has never failed, making it one of the most successful descriptions of nature ever produced. Far from being mere abstraction, its predictions (4) ____ much of modern technology, from the lasers in supermarket scanners to the chips inside our phones. The lesson, perhaps, is that the universe is under no (5) ____ to match the expectations of creatures who evolved to deal with rocks and rivers.

blanks.tr: 'defy common sense' = sağduyuya meydan okumak; kuantumun tuhaflığı.
blanks.en: 'defy common sense' fits quantum strangeness.

blanks.tr: 'in several states at the same time' = aynı anda birkaç durumda; süperpozisyon.
blanks.en: 'at the same time' fits superposition.

blanks.tr: 'difficult to accept' = kabul etmesi güç; tanıdık olmayan sonuçlar.
blanks.en: 'difficult to accept' fits the unfamiliar results.

blanks.tr: 'predictions underpin modern technology' = öngörüler teknolojinin temelini oluşturur.
blanks.en: 'underpin modern technology' fits lasers and chips.

blanks.tr: 'under no obligation to match our expectations' = beklentilerimize uymak zorunda değil.
blanks.en: 'under no obligation' fits the closing point.

cloze.title: Why We Put Things Off
cloze.text: Almost everyone has, at some point, delayed an important task in favour of something easier or more pleasant. Psychologists who study this habit, known as procrastination, argue that it is rarely a simple matter of (1) ____. More often, people put things off because the task makes them feel anxious or bored, and avoiding it brings a short moment of (2) ____. Unfortunately, the task does not disappear, and the stress usually (3) ____ as the deadline approaches. Researchers suggest that the most effective response is not to wait for motivation to appear but to make the first step as (4) ____ as possible, perhaps by promising to work for only five minutes. Once a person has begun, continuing often feels surprisingly easy. Understanding procrastination as an emotional habit rather than a (5) ____ failing can make it far less frightening to overcome.

blanks.tr: 'rarely a simple matter of laziness' = nadiren sadece tembellik meselesi; yaygın yanılgıyı çürütür.
blanks.en: 'a simple matter of laziness' is the myth being corrected.

blanks.tr: 'a short moment of relief' = kısa bir rahatlama anı; kaçınmanın ödülü.
blanks.en: 'a short moment of relief' fits avoidance.

blanks.tr: 'the stress usually grows' = stres genelde artar; erteleme sonucu.
blanks.en: 'the stress usually grows' fits procrastination's cost.

blanks.tr: 'make the first step as small as possible' = ilk adımı olabildiğince küçük yapmak; strateji.
blanks.en: 'as small as possible' fits the recommended strategy.

blanks.tr: 'rather than a moral failing' = ahlaki bir kusur olarak değil; duygusal alışkanlık vurgusu.
blanks.en: 'a moral failing' contrasts with the emotional-habit view.

cloze.title: Across Unknown Seas
cloze.text: In the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, sailors from Europe set out on voyages that would (1) ____ the map of the world. Driven by the hope of profit and the search for new routes to the spices of Asia, they crossed oceans that had never before been (2) ____ by their people. These journeys required real courage, for the ships were small and the dangers were great. The results, however, were enormous and not always happy. Contact between distant continents allowed plants, animals, and ideas to (3) ____ in every direction, changing diets and landscapes forever. At the same time, the arrival of the newcomers often brought disease and conquest to the peoples they (4) ____. The age of exploration, then, must be remembered as a period that was at once (5) ____ and deeply destructive, depending very much on where one stood.

blanks.tr: 'redraw the map of the world' = dünya haritasını yeniden çizmek; keşiflerin etkisi.
blanks.en: 'redraw the map' fits the impact of exploration.

blanks.tr: 'never before been crossed' = daha önce hiç geçilmemiş; bilinmeyen okyanuslar.
blanks.en: 'never before been crossed' fits unknown seas.

blanks.tr: 'allowed plants and ideas to spread' = bitki ve fikirlerin yayılmasını sağladı; değiş tokuş.
blanks.en: 'to spread in every direction' fits the exchange.

blanks.tr: 'the peoples they encountered' = karşılaştıkları halklar; fetih ve hastalık.
blanks.en: 'the peoples they encountered' fits conquest and disease.

blanks.tr: 'at once remarkable and deeply destructive' = hem dikkat çekici hem yıkıcı; çift yönlü değerlendirme.
blanks.en: 'remarkable and deeply destructive' fits the balanced verdict.

cloze.title: Fire and the Forest
cloze.text: To most people, a forest fire is simply a disaster, and in many cases it certainly is. Yet ecologists have come to understand that fire is also a natural part of how some landscapes (1) ____. Certain trees, for instance, produce cones that only open and release their seeds when (2) ____ to intense heat, so that a new generation springs up after the flames have passed. For thousands of years, small, frequent fires cleared away dead wood and kept these systems healthy. Problems arise when humans (3) ____ all fires for long periods, allowing fuel to build up until an eventual blaze becomes far more (4) ____ than any natural one. Managing such landscapes, therefore, is not a matter of removing fire altogether but of restoring something closer to the balance that existed before people tried to (5) ____ it completely.

blanks.tr: 'how some landscapes function' = bazı ekosistemlerin işleyişi; ateşin doğal rolü.
blanks.en: 'how landscapes function' fits fire's natural role.

blanks.tr: 'exposed to intense heat' = yoğun ısıya maruz kalınca; kozalakların açılması.
blanks.en: 'exposed to intense heat' fits seed release.

blanks.tr: 'humans suppress all fires' = insanlar tüm yangınları bastırınca; yakıt birikimi.
blanks.en: 'suppress all fires' fits fuel build-up.

blanks.tr: 'far more destructive' = çok daha yıkıcı; biriken yakıtın sonucu.
blanks.en: 'far more destructive' fits accumulated fuel.

blanks.tr: 'tried to control it completely' = onu tümüyle kontrol etmeye çalışmak; dengeyi bozan tutum.
blanks.en: 'control it completely' fits the disruptive approach.

cloze.title: The Doctor on the Screen
cloze.text: In recent years, more and more patients have begun to see their doctors not in person but through a screen. This practice, known as telemedicine, allows a patient at home to (1) ____ a video call with a nurse or physician many miles away. For people who live far from a hospital or who find travel difficult, the benefits are (2) ____: advice that once required a long journey can now arrive in minutes. Telemedicine is also useful for simple matters, such as checking on a patient's recovery or (3) ____ a repeat prescription. It is not, of course, a complete (4) ____ for the traditional visit, since many conditions still need a physical examination. Used wisely, however, it can free doctors to spend more time with the patients who truly need to be (5) ____ in person.

blanks.tr: 'have a video call' = görüntülü görüşme yapmak; telesağlığın tanımı.
blanks.en: 'have a video call' defines telemedicine.

blanks.tr: 'the benefits are clear' = yararlar açık; uzaktakiler için.
blanks.en: 'the benefits are clear' fits remote patients.

blanks.tr: 'renewing a repeat prescription' = tekrar reçeteyi yenilemek; basit işler.
blanks.en: 'renewing a prescription' fits simple tasks.

blanks.tr: 'not a complete replacement' = tam bir ikame değil; muayene gerektiren durumlar.
blanks.en: 'not a complete replacement' fits cases needing examination.

blanks.tr: 'seen in person' = yüz yüze görülmek; gerçekten gerekli hastalar.
blanks.en: 'seen in person' fits patients who truly need it.

cloze.title: The Crossroads City
cloze.text: For more than a thousand years, the city of Constantinople stood at the meeting point of Europe and Asia, and its wealth (1) ____ heavily on this position. Goods from distant lands passed through its harbours, and the taxes collected on them filled the treasury of the empire. The city's craftsmen were famous for luxury items, especially silk, the secret of whose production the state guarded (2) ____. So great was the flow of trade that the city's coinage became a trusted currency across much of the medieval world, (3) ____ in markets far beyond the empire's borders. Yet such riches also made the city a (4) ____ for ambitious rivals, and its walls were tested again and again. When those defences finally failed, the loss was felt not only locally but across a network of commerce that had (5) ____ on the great crossroads city for centuries.

blanks.tr: 'wealth rested on this position' = zenginlik bu konuma dayanıyordu; coğrafi avantaj.
blanks.en: 'rested on this position' fits geographic advantage.

blanks.tr: 'guarded jealously' = kıskançlıkla korunan ipek sırrı.
blanks.en: 'guarded jealously' fits the silk secret.

blanks.tr: 'accepted in markets far beyond' = uzak pazarlarda kabul edilen; güvenilir para.
blanks.en: 'accepted in distant markets' fits the trusted coinage.

blanks.tr: 'a target for ambitious rivals' = hırslı rakipler için hedef; zenginliğin bedeli.
blanks.en: 'a target for rivals' fits the cost of riches.

blanks.tr: 'a network that had depended on the city' = şehre bağımlı ağ; düşüşün etkisi. 'depend on' kalıbı.
blanks.en: 'depended on the city' fits the trade network's reliance.

cloze.title: The Web of Living Things
cloze.text: A healthy natural area is rarely home to just one or two kinds of plant and animal. Instead, it usually contains a great (1) ____ of species, each connected to the others in countless ways. Scientists use the word biodiversity to describe this richness, and they warn that it is now (2) ____ at an alarming rate. When one species disappears, the effect is rarely limited to that single creature. A predator may lose its prey, a plant may lose the insect that (3) ____ it, and the whole system can become less stable as a result. Protecting biodiversity is not, therefore, simply a matter of saving a few attractive animals; it is about keeping the entire web of life strong enough to (4) ____ the shocks that nature, and human activity, will inevitably bring. For this reason, many scientists regard it as one of the most (5) ____ tasks of our age.

blanks.tr: 'a great variety of species' = büyük bir tür çeşitliliği; biyoçeşitlilik tanımı.
blanks.en: 'a great variety of species' defines biodiversity.

blanks.tr: 'falling at an alarming rate' = endişe verici hızla azalan; uyarı.
blanks.en: 'falling at an alarming rate' fits the warning.

blanks.tr: 'the insect that pollinates it' = onu tozlaştıran böcek; bağlantı örneği.
blanks.en: 'the insect that pollinates it' fits the example of connection.

blanks.tr: 'withstand the shocks' = şoklara dayanmak; istikrar amacı.
blanks.en: 'withstand the shocks' fits the goal of stability.

blanks.tr: 'one of the most important tasks' = en önemli görevlerden biri; sonuç.
blanks.en: 'one of the most important tasks' concludes the passage.

cloze.title: The Tricks of the Mind
cloze.text: We like to believe that our judgements are based on careful thought, but psychologists have shown that the mind takes many (1) ____ that can lead us astray. These mental shortcuts, known as cognitive biases, usually work quickly and without our (2) ____. One of the best known is the tendency to notice and remember only the evidence that supports what we already believe, while quietly (3) ____ anything that does not. Such biases are not a sign of stupidity; even the most intelligent people fall victim to them, often without realising it. The first step towards thinking more clearly is simply to (4) ____ that these tendencies exist, since a danger that is recognised is far easier to guard against. Trained to pause and question their first reaction, people can learn to (5) ____ at least some of the errors that the mind makes so naturally.

blanks.tr: 'the mind takes many shortcuts' = zihin birçok kestirme kullanır; bilişsel önyargı.
blanks.en: 'shortcuts' names cognitive biases.

blanks.tr: 'without our awareness' = farkındalığımız olmadan; otomatik işleyiş.
blanks.en: 'without our awareness' fits automatic operation.

blanks.tr: 'quietly ignoring anything that does not' = desteklemeyeni göz ardı etmek; teyit yanlılığı.
blanks.en: 'ignoring anything that does not' fits confirmation bias.

blanks.tr: 'recognise that these tendencies exist' = bu eğilimleri kabul etmek; ilk adım.
blanks.en: 'recognise that these tendencies exist' is the first step.

blanks.tr: 'avoid at least some of the errors' = hataların bir kısmından kaçınmak; sonuç.
blanks.en: 'avoid at least some of the errors' concludes the point.

restate.stem: Although the report acknowledges that climate change will displace millions of people, it stops short of recommending any binding international agreement.
opts: While the report admits that climate change will drive mass displacement, it does not go so far as to call for a binding international treaty.
The report denies that climate change will force anyone to move and therefore sees no need for an agreement.
The report calls for a binding international agreement precisely because climate change will displace millions.
The report argues that an international agreement would be useless against the displacement caused by climate change.
restate.tr: 'acknowledges ... but stops short of recommending' = kabul eder ama önermeye varmaz; doğru cevap hem iklim kaynaklı göçün kabulünü hem de bağlayıcı anlaşma önerilmemesi çekincesini korur. Çeldiriciler ya kabulü inkâr eder ya da anlaşmayı savunarak anlamı tersine çevirir.
restate.en: 'acknowledges ... but stops short of recommending' keeps both the admission of displacement and the refusal to call for a binding treaty; the distractors either deny the admission or reverse it.

restate.stem: The improvement reported by some patients may owe less to the drug itself than to their expectation that it will work.
opts: The drug is clearly responsible for the improvement that patients report.
The reported improvement might stem more from patients' expectations than from the medicine.
Patients improve only when they have no expectations about the drug.
Patients' expectations have no measurable effect on whether they improve.
restate.tr: 'may owe less to X than to Y' = X'ten çok Y'ye bağlı olabilir; doğru cevap iyileşmenin ilaçtan çok beklentiye bağlı olabileceği karşılaştırmasını korur. Çeldiriciler ilacı tek sorumlu sayar ya da beklentiyi yok sayar.
restate.en: 'may owe less to X than to Y' means it is more due to Y (expectation); the correct option keeps that comparison, while distractors credit the drug or dismiss expectation.

restate.stem: Analysis of the bones suggests that the community relied heavily on fish, rather than on farmed grain as scholars had previously assumed.
opts: The bones confirm the old view that the community lived mainly on farmed grain.
The community ate neither fish nor grain, according to the bones.
The bones show that the community ate mostly fish, contrary to the earlier belief that grain was their main food.
Scholars still believe that grain was more important than fish for this community.
restate.tr: 'relied heavily on fish, rather than grain as scholars had assumed' = balığa dayandı, sanılan tahıla değil; doğru cevap bu karşıtlığı korur. Çeldiriciler eski tahıl görüşünü doğrular ya da her ikisini de reddeder.
restate.en: 'relied on fish, rather than grain as scholars had assumed' contrasts the new finding with the old assumption; the correct option keeps it, while distractors reaffirm the grain view or deny both.

restate.stem: Automation is likely to eliminate many routine jobs, but it may also create new roles that we cannot yet imagine.
opts: Automation will destroy jobs without producing any new ones.
Automation will create new jobs only by preserving the routine ones.
The new roles created by automation are already clearly understood.
Although automation will probably remove many routine jobs, it could also generate new kinds of work that are hard to foresee.
restate.tr: 'likely to eliminate ... but may also create' = hem yok edebilir hem yaratabilir; doğru cevap her iki yönü de korur. Çeldiriciler yaratımı yok sayar ya da yeni rollerin şimdiden bilindiğini iddia ederek 'cannot yet imagine' ile çelişir.
restate.en: 'likely to eliminate ... but may also create' keeps both sides; the correct option preserves them, while distractors drop the job creation or contradict 'cannot yet imagine'.

restate.stem: Scientists cannot predict the exact day a volcano will erupt, but they can often tell when an eruption is becoming more likely.
opts: Though scientists cannot fix the exact date of an eruption, they can frequently detect when one is growing more probable.
Scientists can name the precise day of an eruption well in advance.
Scientists know nothing about when a volcano might erupt.
Volcanic eruptions happen without any warning signs at all.
restate.tr: 'cannot predict the exact day but can tell when more likely' = kesin günü değil ama olasılık artışını söyleyebilir; doğru cevap bu ayrımı korur. Çeldiriciler ya kesin tarih verir ya da hiçbir şey bilinemez diyerek uç noktalara kaçar.
restate.en: 'cannot predict the exact day but can tell when more likely' is preserved; the distractors swing to extremes (exact date vs. no knowledge).

restate.stem: The survey found that people who read regularly as children are more likely to enjoy books as adults.
opts: Childhood reading has no connection with whether adults enjoy books.
According to the survey, regular reading in childhood is linked to a greater enjoyment of books later in life.
Adults who dislike books were always frequent readers in childhood.
The survey proves that reading in childhood guarantees a love of books forever.
restate.tr: 'more likely to enjoy' = olasılık bildirir; doğru cevap çocukluk okumasıyla yetişkin keyfi arasındaki ihtimalli bağı korur. 'guarantees' diyen çeldirici kesinliğe kaçarak abartır; diğeri bağı koparır.
restate.en: 'more likely to enjoy' is probabilistic; the correct option keeps the link, while a distractor overstates it with 'guarantees' and another severs the link.

restate.stem: Rapid economic growth raised average incomes, yet it did little to narrow the gap between the richest and the poorest.
opts: Economic growth both raised incomes and sharply reduced inequality.
Economic growth lowered average incomes while widening inequality.
Although growth lifted average incomes, it had hardly any effect on the divide between rich and poor.
Growth closed the gap between rich and poor without changing average incomes.
restate.tr: 'raised incomes, yet did little to narrow the gap' = gelir arttı ama uçurum daralmadı; doğru cevap bu karşıtlığı korur. Çeldiriciler eşitsizliğin azaldığını ya da gelirin düştüğünü söyleyerek çelişir.
restate.en: 'raised incomes, yet did little to narrow the gap' keeps both; distractors claim inequality fell or incomes dropped.

restate.stem: Speaking two languages from an early age does not delay a child's development, as was once feared, but appears to strengthen certain mental skills.
opts: Learning two languages early seriously slows down a child's development.
Bilingual children develop at exactly the same rate as others, with no advantages.
Children should avoid learning two languages until they are older.
Contrary to earlier fears, early bilingualism does not hold back development and may even enhance some cognitive abilities.
restate.tr: 'does not delay ... but appears to strengthen' = geciktirmez, hatta güçlendirir; doğru cevap iki noktayı da korur. Çeldiriciler eski 'gecikme' korkusunu doğrular ya da avantajı yok sayar.
restate.en: 'does not delay ... but appears to strengthen' keeps both; distractors revive the old fear of delay or ignore the advantage.

restate.stem: Without additional funding, the museum will be forced to reduce its opening hours and cancel several educational programmes.
opts: Unless it obtains more money, the museum will have to cut its hours and drop some of its educational programmes.
The museum will expand its programmes even if it receives no extra money.
The museum has already received the funding it needs to stay open.
Educational programmes are the only thing the museum plans to keep.
restate.tr: 'Without additional funding ... will be forced to reduce/cancel' = ek fon olmazsa kısmak/iptal zorunda; doğru cevap koşul-sonuç bağını korur. Çeldiriciler koşulu tersine çevirir (genişleme / fon zaten alındı).
restate.en: 'Without additional funding ... will be forced to reduce/cancel' keeps the condition-consequence; distractors reverse the condition (expansion / funding already secured).

restate.stem: The cost of solar power has fallen so dramatically that it is now cheaper than coal in many parts of the world.
opts: Solar power remains far more expensive than coal almost everywhere.
Solar power's price has dropped so sharply that, in many regions, it now undercuts coal.
Coal has become cheaper than solar power across most of the globe.
The price of solar power has hardly changed in recent years.
restate.tr: 'fallen so dramatically that it is now cheaper than coal' = öyle düştü ki kömürden ucuz; doğru cevap bu sonucu korur. Çeldiriciler fiyat ilişkisini tersine çevirir ya da düşüşü yok sayar.
restate.en: 'fallen so dramatically that it is now cheaper than coal' is kept; distractors reverse the price relation or deny the drop.

restate.stem: Long periods of stress can weaken the immune system, making people more vulnerable to common infections.
opts: Stress strengthens the immune system and protects people from infection.
Infections are the main cause of long-term stress in most people.
Prolonged stress can lower the body's defences, leaving people more open to ordinary infections.
Stress affects the immune system only over very short periods.
restate.tr: 'weaken the immune system, making more vulnerable' = bağışıklığı zayıflatıp savunmasız bırakır; doğru cevap aynı neden-sonucu korur. Çeldirici tam tersini (güçlendirir) iddia eder.
restate.en: 'weaken the immune system, making more vulnerable' keeps the cause-effect; a distractor claims the opposite (strengthens).

restate.stem: Far from being isolated, the early city maintained extensive contacts with distant regions through a network of trade routes.
opts: The early city was completely cut off from the rest of the world.
Trade routes existed but the city refused to use them.
The city traded only with its immediate neighbours.
Rather than standing alone, the early city was widely connected to far-off regions by trade routes.
restate.tr: 'Far from being isolated ... maintained extensive contacts' = izole olmak şöyle dursun, geniş temaslar; doğru cevap bu vurguyu korur. Çeldiriciler izolasyonu ya da yalnızca komşularla ticareti öne sürerek çelişir.
restate.en: 'Far from being isolated ... maintained extensive contacts' is kept; distractors suggest isolation or trade only with neighbours.

restate.stem: Regular physical activity not only improves fitness but also helps to reduce feelings of anxiety and low mood.
opts: Besides making people fitter, regular exercise can also ease anxiety and lift a low mood.
Exercise improves fitness but has no effect on a person's mood.
Exercise lifts the mood only in people who are already very fit.
Physical activity increases anxiety in most people who try it.
restate.tr: 'not only improves fitness but also reduces anxiety' = hem formu artırır hem kaygıyı azaltır; doğru cevap iki yararı da korur. Çeldiriciler ruh hali etkisini yok sayar ya da yönü tersine çevirir.
restate.en: 'not only improves fitness but also reduces anxiety' keeps both benefits; distractors drop the mood effect or reverse it.

restate.stem: When a language disappears, it is not only words that are lost but also a unique way of understanding the world.
opts: The loss of a language means losing only a list of words.
The death of a language takes with it not merely its vocabulary but a distinctive way of seeing the world.
Languages disappear because their words are no longer useful.
A vanished language can always be fully recovered from its words.
restate.tr: 'not only words ... but also a unique way of understanding' = sadece sözcükler değil, dünyayı anlamanın özgün bir biçimi; doğru cevap bu eklemeyi korur. Çeldirici 'sadece sözcük' diyerek eksiltir.
restate.en: 'not only words ... but also a unique way of understanding' keeps the addition; a distractor reduces it to 'just words'.

restate.stem: Using bright screens late at night can make it harder to fall asleep, because the light interferes with the body's natural rhythms.
opts: Bright screens at night help people fall asleep more quickly.
The body's rhythms have nothing to do with screen light.
Looking at bright screens late at night may delay sleep, since the light disrupts the body's natural rhythms.
People sleep better the more they use screens before bed.
restate.tr: 'make it harder to fall asleep, because the light interferes' = ışık ritmi bozduğu için uykuyu zorlaştırır; doğru cevap neden-sonucu korur. Çeldiriciler tersini (uykuyu kolaylaştırır) iddia eder.
restate.en: 'make it harder to fall asleep, because the light interferes' keeps the cause-effect; distractors claim the opposite.

restate.stem: The fossil record is incomplete, so the absence of a species from a particular layer does not necessarily mean it was extinct at that time.
opts: If a species is missing from a layer, it was certainly extinct then.
The fossil record is complete, so missing species must have been extinct.
Fossils can never tell us anything about when species lived.
Because the fossil record has gaps, a species' absence from a layer does not prove it had died out by then.
restate.tr: 'incomplete, so absence does not necessarily mean extinct' = kayıt eksik olduğundan yokluk mutlaka soy tükenmesi değil; doğru cevap bu temkinli çıkarımı korur. Çeldiriciler yanlış kesinlik ekler.
restate.en: 'incomplete, so absence does not necessarily mean extinct' keeps the cautious inference; distractors add false certainty.

restate.stem: The proposed reform would simplify the tax system, though critics worry that it could reduce the revenue available for public services.
opts: While the reform would make the tax system simpler, opponents fear it might cut the funds available for public services.
The reform would complicate the tax system and increase public revenue.
Everyone agrees the reform would raise more money for public services.
Critics believe the reform would have no effect on public services at all.
restate.tr: 'would simplify ... though critics worry it could reduce revenue' = sadeleştirir ama eleştirmenler geliri azaltabileceğinden kaygılı; doğru cevap iki yönü de korur. Çeldiriciler sadeleştirmeyi ya da kaygıyı tersine çevirir.
restate.en: 'would simplify ... though critics worry it could reduce revenue' keeps both; distractors reverse the simplification or the concern.

restate.stem: Robotic systems can assist surgeons by improving precision, but they are tools that still depend entirely on human judgement.
opts: Robotic systems have replaced surgeons and now operate on their own.
Although robotic systems can make surgery more precise, they remain instruments that rely completely on human decision-making.
Robots make surgery less precise and should not be used.
Human judgement plays no part once a robotic system is used.
restate.tr: 'can assist ... but still depend entirely on human judgement' = yardımcı olur ama tamamen insan kararına bağlı; doğru cevap bu dengeyi korur. Çeldiriciler insan rolünü siler ya da robotu işe yaramaz sayar.
restate.en: 'can assist ... but still depend entirely on human judgement' keeps the balance; distractors erase the human role or dismiss the robots.

restate.stem: Much of the plastic that ends up in the ocean breaks into tiny pieces that are almost impossible to remove.
opts: Plastic in the ocean stays in large pieces that are easy to collect.
The ocean naturally dissolves all the plastic that reaches it.
A large part of ocean plastic fragments into minuscule particles that can scarcely be cleared away.
Removing plastic from the ocean is a simple and quick task.
restate.tr: 'breaks into tiny pieces almost impossible to remove' = temizlemesi neredeyse imkânsız küçük parçalara ayrılır; doğru cevap bunu korur. Çeldiriciler zorluğu yok sayar.
restate.en: 'breaks into tiny pieces almost impossible to remove' is kept; distractors deny the difficulty.

restate.stem: Remote work offers employees greater flexibility, but it can also blur the boundary between professional and personal life.
opts: Remote work removes all flexibility from employees' schedules.
Working from home keeps work and personal life strictly separate.
Remote work has no effect on the balance between work and personal life.
While remote work gives employees more flexibility, it may also make the line between work and home life less clear.
restate.tr: 'offers flexibility, but can blur the boundary' = esneklik sağlar ama sınırı bulanıklaştırabilir; doğru cevap iki yönü de korur. Çeldiriciler esnekliği yok sayar ya da sınırın net kaldığını söyler.
restate.en: 'offers flexibility, but can blur the boundary' keeps both; distractors drop the flexibility or claim the line stays sharp.

restate.stem: Even if emissions were halted today, many glaciers would continue to shrink for decades because of the heat already stored in the oceans.
opts: Glaciers would keep retreating for years even after emissions stopped, owing to heat the oceans have already absorbed.
Stopping emissions now would immediately halt the shrinking of all glaciers.
Glaciers are shrinking only because emissions continue to rise.
The oceans store no heat, so glaciers respond at once to emission cuts.
restate.tr: 'Even if ... halted today ... would continue to shrink ... because of heat already stored' = bugün dursa bile depolanmış ısı yüzünden küçülme sürer; doğru cevap bu gecikmeli etkiyi korur. Diğerleri anında durmayı ya da ısının olmadığını iddia eder.
restate.en: 'Even if halted today ... would continue to shrink because of heat already stored' keeps the lagged effect; distractors claim instant halt or no stored heat.

restate.stem: Public confidence in vaccines depends less on the science itself than on whether people trust the institutions that deliver it.
opts: Vaccine confidence rests entirely on the quality of the science.
People's trust in institutions matters more than the science for vaccine confidence.
Institutions have no influence on whether people accept vaccines.
People reject vaccines only when the science is weak.
restate.tr: 'depends less on the science than on whether people trust the institutions' = bilimsel veriden çok kurumlara güvene bağlı; doğru cevap bu karşılaştırmayı korur. Diğerleri bilime ya da kuruma ağırlığı ters çevirir.
restate.en: 'depends less on the science than on trust in institutions' is kept; distractors reverse the weighting.

restate.stem: Contrary to common belief, densely built cities can be greener than sprawling suburbs, since shorter distances reduce the need for cars.
opts: Dense cities always pollute more than spread-out suburbs.
Suburbs are greener because their houses are far apart.
Despite what many assume, compact cities may be more environmentally friendly than sprawl, as people drive less.
Car use has no connection to how a city is built.
restate.tr: 'Contrary to common belief ... can be greener ... since shorter distances reduce the need for cars' = yaygın inancın aksine yoğun şehir daha yeşil olabilir; doğru cevap bunu korur. Diğerleri ters iddia eder.
restate.en: 'Contrary to common belief, dense cities can be greener since shorter distances cut car use' is kept; distractors invert it.

restate.stem: However impressive its output may seem, a language model does not understand meaning in the way a human does; it predicts likely sequences of words.
opts: A language model understands meaning exactly as a person does.
The model's output is never impressive because it lacks understanding.
Humans and models both produce text without any understanding at all.
Although its results look impressive, such a model predicts probable word sequences rather than grasping meaning like a human.
restate.tr: 'However impressive ... does not understand ... predicts likely sequences' = etkileyici olsa da anlamı kavramaz, olası dizileri tahmin eder; doğru cevap her iki yönü korur.
restate.en: 'However impressive, it predicts word sequences rather than understanding' keeps both halves.

restate.stem: While raising the minimum wage can lift many families out of poverty, economists disagree about whether it also reduces the number of available jobs.
opts: Raising the minimum wage may help poor families, but experts are divided over its effect on job numbers.
Economists fully agree that a higher minimum wage destroys jobs.
A higher minimum wage helps poor families and certainly creates more jobs.
The minimum wage has no effect on poverty or employment.
restate.tr: 'can lift families out of poverty, economists disagree about whether it reduces jobs' = yoksulluğu azaltabilir ama istihdam etkisi tartışmalı; doğru cevap iki yönü de korur.
restate.en: 'lifts families out of poverty, but experts are divided on jobs' keeps both points.

restate.stem: Students who study a little each day tend to remember more than those who try to learn everything the night before an exam.
opts: Cramming the night before leads to better memory than daily study.
Spreading study over many days usually produces better recall than last-minute cramming.
Daily study and last-minute study give exactly the same results.
Memory does not depend on how study is spaced.
restate.tr: 'study a little each day tend to remember more than ... the night before' = günlük çalışma son geceye göre daha iyi hatırlatır; doğru cevap bu karşılaştırmayı korur.
restate.en: 'daily study remembers more than night-before cramming' keeps the comparison.

restate.stem: Although museums argue that they preserve ancient objects for all humanity, many countries insist that such items belong in their place of origin.
opts: Museums and origin countries fully agree on where ancient objects belong.
Origin countries believe ancient objects are safest in foreign museums.
Museums claim to protect objects for everyone, yet many nations maintain the items should return home.
Museums admit that ancient objects belong in their country of origin.
restate.tr: 'museums argue they preserve ... many countries insist they belong in their origin' = müzeler korumayı, ülkeler iadeyi savunur; doğru cevap iki tarafı da korur.
restate.en: 'museums claim to preserve, yet nations insist on return' keeps both sides.

restate.stem: Online learning makes courses available to people who could never attend in person, but it works best when students are already good at managing their own time.
opts: Online learning suits everyone equally, regardless of self-discipline.
Online courses are useless for people who cannot attend in person.
Time management has nothing to do with online learning.
Online courses reach distant learners, yet they succeed most with students who can organise their own time.
restate.tr: 'makes courses available ... but works best when students manage their own time' = uzaktakilere ulaşır ama öz disiplin gerektirir; doğru cevap iki yönü korur.
restate.en: 'reaches distant learners but works best with self-managers' keeps both halves.

restate.stem: The more often antibiotics are used unnecessarily, the faster bacteria develop resistance to them.
opts: Frequent unnecessary use of antibiotics accelerates the development of resistant bacteria.
Using antibiotics rarely speeds up bacterial resistance.
Bacteria become resistant only when antibiotics are never used.
Antibiotic use has no effect on resistance.
restate.tr: 'the more often ... unnecessarily, the faster bacteria develop resistance' = gereksiz kullanım arttıkça direnç hızlanır; doğru cevap bu orantıyı korur.
restate.en: 'the more unnecessary use, the faster resistance' keeps the proportional link.

restate.stem: Solar and wind power are now cheap to generate, but their value is limited until we can store the electricity for times when the sun is down and the wind is still.
opts: Solar and wind power are expensive and rarely worth using.
Cheap as they are to produce, solar and wind reach their full value only once we can store their electricity for calm, dark periods.
Storing electricity is unnecessary for solar and wind power.
The sun and wind provide constant, uninterrupted power.
restate.tr: 'cheap to generate, but value limited until we can store ... for times when sun is down' = üretimi ucuz ama depolama olmadan değeri sınırlı; doğru cevap bunu korur.
restate.en: 'cheap to generate but limited until stored' keeps the condition.

restate.stem: When the last fluent speaker of a language dies, the knowledge encoded in that language — its songs, names, and ways of describing the world — usually vanishes with them.
opts: A language survives easily even after its last speaker dies.
Only the grammar of a language is lost when its last speaker dies.
The death of a language's last speaker generally erases the unique knowledge that language carried.
Songs and names are always recorded before a language disappears.
restate.tr: 'when the last speaker dies, the knowledge ... usually vanishes with them' = son konuşmacıyla o bilgi yok olur; doğru cevap kapsamı korur.
restate.en: 'with the last speaker, the encoded knowledge vanishes' keeps the scope.

restate.stem: Regular physical exercise benefits not only the body but also the brain, improving memory and concentration.
