translate.tr: 'rarely the result of a single cause; diet, exercise, and stress all play a part' = tek nedenli değil, hepsi rol oynar; doğru çeviri çoklu nedeni korur. Çeldiriciler tek nedene indirger.
translate.en: 'rarely a single cause; diet, exercise, stress all play a part' is kept; distractors reduce it to one cause.

translate.source: The hunting of these animals has been banned for years, yet their numbers continue to fall because their habitat is shrinking.
opts: Bu hayvanların avlanması yıllardır yasak olmasına rağmen, yaşam alanları daraldığı için sayıları düşmeye devam ediyor.
Bu hayvanların sayısı, avlanma yasağı sayesinde hızla artmaktadır.
Yaşam alanlarının daralması bu hayvanlara zarar vermez.
Avlanma yasağı, hayvanların sayısını tamamen eski hâline getirmiştir.
translate.tr: 'banned for years, yet their numbers continue to fall because their habitat is shrinking' = yasağa rağmen yaşam alanı daraldığından sayı düşer; doğru çeviri karşıtlık ve nedeni korur.
translate.en: 'banned, yet numbers fall because habitat shrinks' keeps the contrast and cause.

translate.source: By raising interest rates, the central bank hopes to slow inflation, even though doing so may also slow economic growth.
opts: Merkez bankası, ekonomik büyümeyi hızlandırmak için faiz oranlarını düşürüyor.
Merkez bankası, faiz oranlarını artırarak enflasyonu yavaşlatmayı umuyor; ancak bunun ekonomik büyümeyi de yavaşlatabileceğinin farkında.
Faiz artışı enflasyonu yükseltmek amacıyla yapılır.
Faiz oranları ekonomik büyümeyi hiçbir biçimde etkilemez.
translate.tr: 'raising rates ... to slow inflation, even though it may slow growth' = enflasyonu yavaşlatmak için faiz artırır, büyümeyi de yavaşlatabilir; doğru çeviri amaç-ödün dengesini korur.
translate.en: 'raising rates to slow inflation, even though it may slow growth' keeps the aim-tradeoff.

translate.source: The more conveniently a service tracks our preferences, the more personal information we quietly hand over to it.
opts: Bir hizmet tercihlerimizi takip etse bile ona hiç kişisel bilgi vermeyiz.
Bir hizmet tercihlerimizi ne kadar kolaylıkla takip ederse, ona o kadar çok kişisel bilgiyi farkında olmadan veririz.
Hizmetler ne kadar bilgi toplarsa o kadar az işe yararlar.
translate.tr: 'The more conveniently ... tracks, the more information we hand over' = ne kadar kolay takip ederse o kadar bilgi veririz; doğru çeviri 'the more ... the more' kalıbını korur.
translate.en: 'the more it tracks, the more we hand over' keeps the correlative structure.

translate.source: When fishing is forbidden in certain areas of the sea, fish populations there often recover quickly and spread to neighbouring waters.
opts: Balıkçılık yasaklandığında balık sayısı her zaman azalır.
Balık popülasyonları yalnızca avlanma serbest olduğunda artar.
Korunan bölgelerdeki balıklar asla başka sulara geçmez.
Denizin belirli bölgelerinde balıkçılık yasaklandığında, oradaki balık popülasyonları çoğu zaman hızla toparlanır ve komşu sulara yayılır.
translate.tr: 'fishing forbidden ... populations recover quickly and spread to neighbouring waters' = yasakla popülasyon toparlanıp yayılır; doğru çeviri neden-sonucu korur.
translate.en: 'fishing forbidden, populations recover and spread' keeps the cause-effect.

translate.source: Online courses have made learning available to people who, only a generation ago, would never have had the chance to study.
opts: Çevrimiçi kurslar, daha bir kuşak önce okuma fırsatı asla bulamayacak insanlar için öğrenmeyi erişilebilir kıldı.
Çevrimiçi kurslar yalnızca zaten üniversiteye gidenler için yararlıdır.
Bir kuşak önce herkesin okuma fırsatı vardı.
Çevrimiçi kurslar öğrenmeyi daha da zorlaştırmıştır.
translate.tr: 'made learning available to people who ... would never have had the chance' = fırsatı olmayanlara öğrenmeyi açtı; doğru çeviri bu erişimi korur.
translate.en: 'made learning available to people who would never have had the chance' keeps the access point.

translate.source: Many people believe they can catch up on lost sleep at the weekend, but research suggests this does not fully repair the damage.
opts: Araştırmalar, hafta sonu uykusunun tüm zararı tamamen giderdiğini kanıtlamıştır.
Birçok kişi kaybettiği uykuyu hafta sonu telafi edebileceğine inanır, ama araştırmalar bunun zararı tam olarak gidermediğini gösteriyor.
Kaybedilen uyku vücuda hiçbir zarar vermez.
translate.tr: 'believe they can catch up ... but research suggests this does not fully repair the damage' = telafi edilebileceği sanılır ama araştırma tam onarmadığını gösterir; doğru çeviri karşıtlığı korur.
translate.en: 'believe they can catch up, but research says it doesn't fully repair' keeps the contrast.

translate.source: Planting trees along city streets does more than improve the view; it lowers temperatures, cleans the air, and lifts people's mood.
opts: Şehir sokaklarına ağaç dikmek yalnızca manzarayı güzelleştirir.
Ağaçlar şehirde sıcaklığı yükseltir ve havayı kirletir.
Şehir sokaklarına ağaç dikmek manzarayı güzelleştirmekten fazlasını yapar; sıcaklığı düşürür, havayı temizler ve insanların ruh hâlini iyileştirir.
Sokak ağaçlarının insanların ruh hâliyle hiçbir ilgisi yoktur.
translate.tr: 'does more than improve the view; it lowers temperatures, cleans the air, and lifts mood' = manzaradan fazlası; doğru çeviri üç yararı da korur. Çeldiriciler tek yarara indirger ya da ters çevirir.
translate.en: 'does more than the view; lowers temperatures, cleans air, lifts mood' keeps all three benefits.

translate.source: Kazılarda bulunan tahıl kalıntıları, bu topluluğun düşünüldüğünden çok daha önce yerleşik tarıma geçtiğini ortaya koymaktadır.
opts: The grain remains show that this community never practised any farming.
The excavations found no grain remains belonging to this community.
This community took up farming much later than researchers had assumed.
The grain remains found during the excavations reveal that this community took up settled farming far earlier than had been thought.
translate.tr: 'düşünüldüğünden çok daha önce yerleşik tarıma geçtiğini' = took up settled farming far earlier than had been thought; doğru çeviri bunu korur. 'much later' diyen çeldirici tersine çevirir.
translate.en: 'took up settled farming far earlier than had been thought' is kept; 'much later' reverses it.

translate.source: Araştırmacılar, ilacın işe yaradığını iddia etmeden önce sonuçların bağımsız ekiplerce doğrulanması gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır.
opts: Researchers stress that the results must be confirmed by independent teams before any claim is made that the drug works.
Researchers claim the drug has already been proven to work by everyone.
Researchers argue that no confirmation of the results is necessary.
Researchers say the drug definitely does not work.
translate.tr: 'iddia etmeden önce bağımsız ekiplerce doğrulanması gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır' = must be confirmed by independent teams before any claim; doğru çeviri koşulu korur.
translate.en: 'must be confirmed by independent teams before any claim' keeps the condition.

translate.source: Bir ülkenin uzun vadeli refahı, yalnızca doğal kaynaklarına değil, aynı zamanda eğitimli iş gücüne de bağlıdır.
opts: A country's prosperity depends solely on its natural resources.
A country's long-term prosperity depends not only on its natural resources but also on its educated workforce.
An educated workforce has no effect on a country's prosperity.
Natural resources are the only thing that matters for prosperity.
translate.tr: 'yalnızca ... değil, aynı zamanda ... de' = not only ... but also ...; doğru çeviri çift vurguyu korur. Çeldiriciler tek etkene indirger.
translate.en: 'not only ... but also ...' keeps the double emphasis; distractors reduce it to one factor.

translate.source: Otomasyon birçok rutin işi ortadan kaldırsa da, henüz hayal bile edemediğimiz yeni meslekler yaratabilir.
opts: Automation will destroy jobs without ever creating any new ones.
The new professions created by automation are already well understood.
Although automation may eliminate many routine jobs, it could create new professions that we cannot yet even imagine.
Automation has no effect on the kinds of jobs available.
translate.tr: 'kaldırsa da ... hayal bile edemediğimiz yeni meslekler yaratabilir' = although it eliminates ... it could create jobs we cannot yet imagine; doğru çeviri ödün yapısını korur.
translate.en: 'although it eliminates jobs, it could create ones we cannot yet imagine' keeps the concessive structure.

translate.source: Plastiğin denizlerde parçalanması yüzyıllar alabilir ve bu süre boyunca sayısız deniz canlısına zarar verir.
opts: Plastic breaks down in the sea within a few days and harms nothing.
Marine creatures are not affected by plastic in any way.
Plastic disappears from the sea almost immediately.
Plastic can take centuries to break down in the sea, and during that time it harms countless marine creatures.
translate.tr: 'parçalanması yüzyıllar alabilir ve bu süre boyunca zarar verir' = can take centuries to break down and harms during that time; doğru çeviri süre ve zararı korur.
translate.en: 'can take centuries to break down and harms during that time' keeps the duration and harm.

translate.source: Matbaanın icadı, yalnızca kitapların değil, aynı zamanda yeni düşüncelerin de eskisinden çok daha hızlı yayılmasını sağladı.
opts: The invention of printing allowed not only books but also new ideas to spread far faster than before.
The invention of printing slowed the spread of books and ideas.
Printing had no effect on how quickly ideas spread.
Only books, never ideas, were affected by printing.
translate.tr: 'yalnızca kitapların değil, aynı zamanda yeni düşüncelerin de ... çok daha hızlı yayılmasını sağladı' = allowed not only books but also ideas to spread far faster; doğru çeviri bunu korur.
translate.en: 'allowed not only books but also ideas to spread far faster' is kept.

translate.source: İnsanların bir kaybın acısını, eşdeğer bir kazancın verdiği mutluluktan çok daha güçlü hissettiği gösterilmiştir.
opts: It has been shown that people care equally about losses and gains.
It has been shown that people feel the pain of a loss far more strongly than the pleasure of an equal gain.
People feel gains far more strongly than losses, studies show.
Losses and gains have no emotional effect on people.
translate.tr: 'bir kaybın acısını ... eşdeğer kazancın mutluluğundan çok daha güçlü hissettiği' = feel the pain of a loss far more strongly than the pleasure of an equal gain; doğru çeviri karşılaştırmayı korur.
translate.en: 'feel the pain of a loss far more than the pleasure of an equal gain' keeps the comparison.

translate.source: Büyük şehirlerde yaşayan insanlar, komşularını çoğu zaman küçük kasabalardakinden çok daha az tanır.
opts: People in big cities always know their neighbours better than those in small towns.
People in small towns rarely know their neighbours at all.
People who live in big cities often know their neighbours far less well than those in small towns.
City and town residents know their neighbours equally well.
translate.tr: 'komşularını ... küçük kasabalardakinden çok daha az tanır' = know their neighbours far less than those in small towns; doğru çeviri karşılaştırmayı korur. Çeldirici 'better' ile ters çevirir.
translate.en: 'know their neighbours far less than those in small towns' is kept; 'better' reverses it.

translate.source: Erken teşhis, birçok hastalıkta tedavinin başarı şansını önemli ölçüde artırdığı için hayati öneme sahiptir.
opts: Early diagnosis makes treatment less likely to succeed.
Early diagnosis has no effect on the success of treatment.
Treatment succeeds only when diagnosis is made as late as possible.
Early diagnosis is vital because, in many diseases, it significantly increases the chances that treatment will succeed.
translate.tr: 'tedavinin başarı şansını önemli ölçüde artırdığı için hayati öneme sahiptir' = vital because it significantly increases the chances treatment succeeds; doğru çeviri nedeni korur.
translate.en: 'vital because it significantly increases the chance treatment succeeds' keeps the reason.

errorhunt.text: Recycling have become an important part of modern life. Last year alone, our school collect more than two tonnes of paper for reuse. When we recycle glass and metal, we save energy and protect the environment at the same time. Such small actions, repeated by many people, can make a real difference to the planet in long term, and to the generations who will live here after us.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'Recycling' tekil sayılır, yardımcı fiil 'has' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'Recycling' is singular, so it takes 'has'.

errors.tr: Zaman: 'Last year' geçmişi gösterir, fiil 'collected' (geçmiş zaman) olmalı.
errors.en: Tense: 'Last year' signals the past, so the verb must be 'collected'.

errors.tr: Eksik tanımlık: kalıp 'in the long term' biçimindedir.
errors.en: Missing article: the fixed phrase is 'in the long term'.

errorhunt.text: Doing regular exercise are one of the best ways to stay healthy. My doctor often tells me that I should move more and to sit less during the day. Even a short walk can improve your mood and is good for the heart. If we make exercise a habit while we are young, it becomes much easier to keep it up later of life.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: özne 'Doing regular exercise' tekildir, fiil 'is' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: the subject 'Doing regular exercise' is singular, so 'is'.

errors.tr: Koşut yapı: 'move' yalın fiille eşlenmeli; 'to' fazladır ('move more and sit less').
errors.en: Parallel structure: it should match 'move' with the bare verb; 'to' is wrong ('move more and sit less').

errors.tr: Edat hatası: kalıp 'later in life' biçimindedir.
errors.en: Preposition error: the phrase is 'later in life'.

errorhunt.text: The internet has change the way we find information completely. Twenty years ago, a student had to spend hours in a library, but now answers appears in seconds. Of course, not everything we read online is true, so we must always check our sources with care. Learning how to do this is one of the most important skill in the modern world.

errors.tr: Zaman/ortaç: present perfect 'has' ile fiilin üçüncü hâli 'changed' kullanılır.
errors.en: Tense/participle: present perfect 'has' needs the past participle 'changed'.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'answers' çoğuldur, fiil 'appear' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'answers' is plural, so 'appear'.

errors.tr: Sayı: 'one of the most important' kalıbından sonra çoğul 'skills' gelir.
errors.en: Number: 'one of the most important' must be followed by a plural, 'skills'.

errorhunt.text: Getting enough sleep is more important than many people realizes. Last night I slept very badly, and today I cannot barely keep my eyes open. People who sleep less than six hours often feel tired and find it hard to concentrate in their work. Doctors say that going to bed at a regular time helps the body to rest properly.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'people' çoğuldur, fiil 'realize' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'people' is plural, so 'realize'.

errors.tr: Çifte olumsuzluk: 'barely' zaten olumsuzdur; 'cannot' yanlıştır, 'can barely' doğrudur.
errors.en: Double negative: 'barely' is already negative; it should be 'can barely', not 'cannot barely'.

errors.tr: Edat hatası: 'concentrate' fiili 'on' edatıyla kullanılır.
errors.en: Preposition error: 'concentrate' is used with 'on'.

errorhunt.text: Scientists has warned for decades that the planet is growing warmer. The evidence, drawn from many independent sources, is now very difficult to deny. Since the nineteenth century, average temperatures rose steadily, and the rate of change is increasing rapid. If we do not act soon, future generations will inherit a world far less stable than the one we know today.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'Scientists' çoğuldur, yardımcı fiil 'have' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'Scientists' is plural, so 'have'.

errors.tr: Zaman: 'Since the nineteenth century' present perfect ister ('have risen').
errors.en: Tense: 'Since the nineteenth century' requires the present perfect ('have risen').

errors.tr: Kelime formu: fiili niteleyen sözcük zarf olmalı ('rapidly').
errors.en: Word form: the word modifying the verb must be an adverb ('rapidly').

errorhunt.text: The study of history is not only about memorising dates and names. It help us to understand why societies change and how people in past lived their daily lives. A good historian must examine many sources, because a single document can gives a one-sided view of events. By comparing different accounts, we build a picture that is far more balanced than any one source alone.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: özne 'It' tekildir, fiil 'helps' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: the subject 'It' is singular, so 'helps'.

errors.tr: Eksik tanımlık: kalıp 'in the past' biçimindedir.
errors.en: Missing article: the phrase is 'in the past'.

errors.tr: Kip+fiil: 'can' kipinden sonra fiilin yalın hâli ('give') gelir.
errors.en: Modal + verb: after the modal 'can', use the base form 'give'.

errorhunt.text: Washing your hands properly is one of the simplest way to stop the spread of disease. For a long time, doctors did not understood why so many patients fell ill in hospitals. Then a careful physician noticed that washing the hands between visits dramatically reduced infections. Today this habit seem obvious, yet it took many years before the medical world accepted such a simple idea.

errors.tr: Sayı: 'one of the simplest' kalıbından sonra çoğul 'ways' gelir.
errors.en: Number: 'one of the simplest' must be followed by a plural, 'ways'.

errors.tr: Yardımcı fiil+fiil: 'did' ile fiilin yalın hâli ('understand') kullanılır.
errors.en: Auxiliary + verb: with 'did', use the base form 'understand'.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'this habit' tekildir, fiil 'seems' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'this habit' is singular, so 'seems'.

errorhunt.text: When prices rise quickly, the money in people's pockets buy less than it did before. Economists call this problem inflation, and it can quickly damage trust in currency. Governments often respond by raising interest rates, which they hope will slow the economy. However, if they act too strong, they may cause the very recession that they were trying to avoid.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: gerçek özne 'the money' tekildir, fiil 'buys' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: the real subject 'the money' is singular, so 'buys'.

errors.tr: Eksik tanımlık: sayılabilir tekil 'currency' önünde 'a' gerekir.
errors.en: Missing article: the singular countable 'currency' needs 'a'.

errors.tr: Kelime formu: fiili niteleyen sözcük zarf olmalı ('strongly').
errors.en: Word form: the word modifying the verb must be an adverb ('strongly').

errorhunt.text: A balanced diet provide the body with everything it needs to work well. Many people believe that cutting out an entire food group is the fastest way to lose weight, but this often does more harm than good. Instead, doctors advise us eat a wide variety of foods every day. By making small, lasting changes, we are far more likely to stay healthy on the long run.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'A balanced diet' tekildir, fiil 'provides' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'A balanced diet' is singular, so 'provides'.

errors.tr: Fiil yapısı: 'advise somebody to do' kalıbında 'to' gerekir.
errors.en: Verb pattern: 'advise somebody to do' requires 'to'.

errors.tr: Edat hatası: kalıp 'in the long run' biçimindedir.
errors.en: Preposition error: the phrase is 'in the long run'.

errorhunt.text: Over the past decade, smartphones has transformed the way we communicate. A device that was once used only for phone calls now lets us read the news and find our way across unfamiliar city. Yet these benefits come at a price, because we spend more time to look at screens than ever before. Some researchers worry that this constant habit is slowly changing how our brains work.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: 'smartphones' çoğuldur, yardımcı fiil 'have' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: 'smartphones' is plural, so 'have'.

errors.tr: Eksik tanımlık: sayılabilir tekil 'city' önünde 'an' gerekir.
errors.en: Missing article: the singular countable 'city' needs 'an'.

errors.tr: Fiil formu: 'spend time' yapısından sonra '-ing' (looking) gelir.
errors.en: Verb form: 'spend time' is followed by the -ing form ('looking').

errorhunt.text: When schools first begun to use computers, many teachers worried that students would stop to think for themselves. These fears have not entirely disappeared, but most teachers now see technology as a helpful tool rather than a threat. Used wisely, a laptop can give a child access of knowledge that earlier generations could only imagine. The real challenge lies in how these tools are used in the classroom.

errors.tr: Zaman: düzensiz fiilin geçmiş hâli 'began'dır ('begun' geçmiş ortaçtır).
errors.en: Tense: the past simple of the irregular verb is 'began' ('begun' is the past participle).

errors.tr: Fiil yapısı: 'stop doing' (bırakmak) anlamı için '-ing' gerekir.
errors.en: Verb pattern: 'stop doing' (to cease) requires the -ing form.

errors.tr: Edat hatası: 'access' ismi 'to' edatıyla kullanılır.
errors.en: Preposition error: the noun 'access' is used with 'to'.

errorhunt.text: Every summer, the number of forest fires seem to grow larger. Scientists explain that hotter, drier weather creates the conditions for flames to spread quick. In the past, small natural fires cleared away dead wood, but for decades people have put almost all of them out. As a result, fuel builds up, and when a fire finally starts, it burns with a fierce intensity than it once would have.

errors.tr: Özne-yüklem uyumu: gerçek özne 'the number' tekildir, fiil 'seems' olmalı.
errors.en: Subject-verb agreement: the real subject 'the number' is singular, so 'seems'.

errors.tr: Kelime formu: fiili niteleyen sözcük zarf olmalı ('quickly').
errors.en: Word form: the word modifying the verb must be an adverb ('quickly').

errors.tr: Karşılaştırma: 'than' ile karşılaştırma sıfatı 'fiercer' kullanılır.
errors.en: Comparative: 'than' requires the comparative form 'fiercer'.

paraphrase.source: Although the team had practised hard, they lost the final.
paraphrase.instruction: Cümleyi anlamını koruyarak 'despite' ile yeniden yaz.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence with 'despite', keeping the meaning.
paraphrase.sample: Despite practising hard, the team lost the final.

paraphrase.source: Although it was raining heavily, the outdoor festival continued.
paraphrase.instruction: 'despite' kullanarak cümleyi yeniden yaz (bir isim öbeği ile).
paraphrase.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence with 'despite', using a noun phrase.
paraphrase.sample: Despite the heavy rain, the outdoor festival continued.

paraphrase.source: Workers built the new bridge in only two years.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Change the sentence into the passive voice.
paraphrase.sample: The new bridge was built in only two years.

paraphrase.source: Scientists have discovered a new species of frog in the forest.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Change the sentence into the passive voice (present perfect).
paraphrase.sample: A new species of frog has been discovered in the forest.

paraphrase.source: I met a woman yesterday. She speaks five languages.
paraphrase.instruction: İki cümleyi 'who' ile bir relative clause olarak birleştir.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Join the two sentences into one using a 'who' relative clause.
paraphrase.sample: Yesterday I met a woman who speaks five languages.

paraphrase.source: This is the village. My grandparents grew up there.
paraphrase.instruction: İki cümleyi 'where' kullanarak tek cümlede birleştir.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Combine the two sentences into one using 'where'.
paraphrase.sample: This is the village where my grandparents grew up.

paraphrase.source: He said, "I will call you tomorrow."
paraphrase.instruction_en: Change the sentence into reported speech.
paraphrase.sample: He said that he would call me the next day.

paraphrase.source: She asked me, "Are you coming to the party?"
paraphrase.instruction_en: Change the question into reported speech.
paraphrase.sample: She asked me whether I was coming to the party.

paraphrase.source: I had never seen such a beautiful sunset before.
paraphrase.instruction: Cümleyi 'Never' ile başlatıp devrik (inversion) yapı kullanarak yeniden yaz.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence beginning with 'Never', using inversion.
paraphrase.sample: Never before had I seen such a beautiful sunset.

paraphrase.source: As soon as we had arrived, the rain started.
paraphrase.instruction: Cümleyi 'No sooner' ile başlatıp devrik yapı kullanarak yeniden yaz.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence beginning with 'No sooner', using inversion.
paraphrase.sample: No sooner had we arrived than the rain started.

paraphrase.source: If you practise more, you will improve faster.
paraphrase.instruction: Cümleyi 'The more ..., the ...' karşılaştırma kalıbıyla yeniden yaz.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence using 'The more ..., the ...'.
paraphrase.sample: The more you practise, the faster you will improve.

paraphrase.source: No other mountain in the range is as high as this one.
paraphrase.instruction: Cümleyi karşılaştırmalı (comparative) yapı kullanarak yeniden yaz, anlamı koru.
paraphrase.instruction_en: Rewrite the sentence using a comparative structure, keeping the meaning.
paraphrase.sample: This mountain is higher than any other in the range.

reading.title: The Case for a Four-Day Week
reading.body:
Many companies are now considering a shorter working week, and there are strong reasons to believe it would benefit both employees and employers.

First, well-rested workers tend to be more productive. When people have an extra day to recover, they return to their desks with more energy and concentration, so the same amount of work can be completed in fewer hours.

Second, a four-day week would reduce a company's running costs. Offices that close one extra day each week use less electricity, heating, and water, and these savings can be considerable over a year.

Finally, the change would be good for the environment. With one fewer day of commuting, fewer cars would be on the road, cutting both traffic and pollution across the city.

lecture.body: Now, the reading makes the four-day week sound wonderful, but I'd be careful before getting too excited. Take the first point, about productivity. The thing is, when you cut a day, the same workload doesn't just disappear. In a lot of cases, employees end up cramming five days of tasks into four, which actually raises stress and can lower the quality of their work, not improve it. Second, those cost savings. They sound nice, but a lot of an office's expenses are fixed — the rent, the software, the insurance — and these don't fall just because the lights are off one extra day. Some firms even have to hire more staff to cover the missing day, which costs more, not less. And finally, this idea about the environment. People often forget that a free day off doesn't mean people stay home. Many use that extra day to drive somewhere, go shopping, or travel for leisure, so the reduction in pollution can be far smaller than the reading suggests.

toeflint.prompt: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on the specific points made in the reading passage.
keyPoints: Workers may cram five days of work into four, raising stress instead of productivity.
Many office costs are fixed and do not fall, and extra staff may even be needed.
People often drive on their day off, so pollution may not drop as expected.

reading.title: Electric Cars as a Clean Solution
reading.body:
Switching from petrol vehicles to electric cars is often presented as the answer to pollution in our cities, and the argument rests on three main points.

To begin with, electric cars produce no exhaust fumes. As they run, they release none of the gases that make city air unhealthy, so replacing petrol cars would clearly improve the air people breathe.

In addition, electric cars are cheaper to run. Electricity costs less than petrol for the same distance, and the motors have fewer parts that can break, so drivers save money over time.

Moreover, the technology helps fight climate change. Because electric cars use no petrol, the total amount of carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere would fall sharply.

lecture.body: So the passage is very positive about electric cars, but the picture is more complicated than it lets on. Let's start with the air pollution claim. Yes, the car itself has no exhaust, but the electricity to charge it has to come from somewhere. If a city's power still comes mainly from burning coal or gas, you've simply moved the pollution from the street to the power station. Now, on the question of cost. Electricity may be cheaper per kilometre, that's true, but these cars are far more expensive to buy in the first place, and the battery often has to be replaced after some years at a very high price. For many families, the total cost is not lower at all. And about climate change — building the batteries is the catch. Mining and processing the metals they need uses huge amounts of energy and damages the land, so the carbon savings are smaller, and slower to appear, than the reading claims.

toeflint.prompt: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on the specific points made in the reading passage.
keyPoints: The electricity may come from coal or gas, moving pollution to the power station.
High purchase price and costly battery replacement can outweigh the cheaper running cost.
Mining and making batteries uses much energy, reducing the climate benefit.

reading.title: Why the Museum Should Charge for Entry
reading.body:
The city museum, which is currently free, is considering charging visitors a small admission fee. Supporters of the plan give several reasons why this would help the museum.

First, the fee would provide much-needed income. The money collected could be used to repair the building, buy new exhibits, and pay the staff properly, all of which the museum struggles to afford today.

Second, a charge would reduce overcrowding. On busy days the galleries are so full that it is hard to see anything, and a fee would mean fewer but more serious visitors.

Third, people tend to value what they pay for. Visitors who have bought a ticket are likely to take the exhibits more seriously and behave more respectfully inside the museum.

lecture.body: The reading lists some neat-sounding benefits of charging for the museum, but I don't think they hold up. Take the income argument first. It assumes the same number of people will keep coming once there's a charge, but that almost never happens. Attendance usually drops sharply when a free museum starts charging, and with far fewer visitors, the total income can actually fall, not rise. Second, this idea about overcrowding. Sure, fewer people would come — but the museum's whole purpose is to bring art and history to as many citizens as possible. Cutting the crowd by shutting out families who can't easily pay isn't a success; it's the museum failing at its main job. And the third point, that people value what they pay for? There's really no good evidence for that. Plenty of visitors treat free galleries with great respect, and charging a fee mostly just keeps out the people who would have benefited most.

toeflint.prompt: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on the specific points made in the reading passage.
keyPoints: Attendance usually falls when a free museum starts charging, so income may drop, not rise.
Reducing the crowd by excluding those who cannot pay undermines the museum's main purpose.
There is little evidence that paying makes visitors more respectful; free galleries are respected too.

toeflint.topic: Was the stone circle an ancient observatory?

reading.title: An Ancient Astronomical Observatory
reading.body:
A famous prehistoric stone circle has long puzzled archaeologists. One popular theory argues that it was built mainly as an astronomical observatory, used to track the movements of the sun and stars.

The strongest evidence is alignment. On the longest day of the year, the sun rises exactly over one particular stone, a coincidence that seems far too precise to be accidental.

Supporters also point to the enormous effort involved. Moving such massive stones over long distances would only have been worthwhile for a purpose of the highest importance, such as marking the seasons for farming.

Finally, similar circles elsewhere show comparable alignments, suggesting that the builders shared a deliberate astronomical tradition.

lecture.body: This observatory theory is appealing, but the evidence is weaker than it first appears. Let's begin with that famous sunrise alignment. Here's the problem: a circle has so many stones and so many gaps that, by pure chance, some of them are bound to line up with the sunrise, the sunset, or a bright star on some important day. Point a line in almost any direction and it will match something in the sky. So a single alignment proves very little. Now, the argument from effort. Yes, moving the stones took enormous work — but people throughout history have made huge efforts for religious or social reasons, not scientific ones. A temple or a meeting place for ceremonies would explain the effort just as well, without any astronomy. And as for the similar circles elsewhere, that's not strong support either. Shared building styles usually spread because of shared culture and religion, and they tell us almost nothing about whether the people inside were studying the stars.

toeflint.prompt: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on the specific points made in the reading passage.
keyPoints: With many stones, some alignment with the sky is likely by chance and proves little.
The huge effort could equally reflect religious or social motives rather than science.
Similar circles elsewhere may share culture or religion, not an astronomical purpose.

reading.title: The Productivity Gains of Remote Work
reading.body:
Since many companies began allowing employees to work from home, supporters have argued that the change makes workforces more productive, for several reasons.

First, remote workers avoid the daily commute. The hours once lost travelling to and from an office can now be spent working or resting, leaving employees fresher and more efficient.

Second, home offers fewer interruptions. Without colleagues stopping by to chat or constant meetings, workers can concentrate deeply on difficult tasks for longer periods.

Third, remote work widens the pool of talent. A company can hire the best people from anywhere in the country, rather than only those who live close enough to travel in each day.

lecture.body: The reading is confident that working from home boosts productivity, but each of its points deserves a second look. Start with the commute. It's true people save travel time, but that time doesn't automatically go into work. At home, there are children, household chores, deliveries — endless small distractions that an office simply doesn't have, and these can eat up far more than the commute ever did. Second, the claim about fewer interruptions. In practice, a lot of the quick, useful exchanges that used to happen in person now turn into long chains of messages and video calls, which are slower and more tiring. Deep concentration isn't guaranteed just because you're alone. And the third point, hiring from anywhere — that may help the company find talent, but it says nothing about whether each worker is more productive. In fact, managing a team spread across many places is harder, communication slips, and projects can move more slowly, not faster.

toeflint.prompt: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on the specific points made in the reading passage.
keyPoints: Saved commute time is often lost to household distractions that offices lack.
Face-to-face exchanges become slow message chains and calls, harming concentration.
Hiring from anywhere does not raise individual output and makes teams harder to manage.

toeflint.topic: Reintroducing wolves to a national park

reading.title: Bringing Back the Wolves
reading.body:
Conservationists have proposed returning wolves to a national park where they were hunted to extinction long ago. They argue that this reintroduction would benefit the whole ecosystem.

To begin with, wolves would control the deer population. With no large predators, deer have multiplied and stripped the land of young trees, and wolves would restore a natural balance.

Furthermore, the return of wolves would help other species recover. As forests regrow, birds, insects, and beavers would all find new habitats, increasing the park's biodiversity.

Lastly, the wolves would attract visitors. Tourists eager to see or hear wild wolves would bring valuable income to the towns around the park.

lecture.body: This plan to bring back the wolves sounds wonderful on paper, but it overlooks some serious difficulties. Take the first claim, about controlling the deer. The trouble is that a small group of released wolves rarely makes a big dent in a deer population spread over a huge area. The deer simply move to places the wolves don't patrol, so the young trees may keep disappearing anyway. Now, the idea that other species will bounce back. That assumes the forest recovers quickly, but in reality these changes can take many decades, and other factors — climate, disease, human activity — often matter far more than the presence of a few predators. And on the tourism point: yes, some visitors are curious, but wolves are shy and are almost never seen. More importantly, farmers living nearby tend to oppose the plan strongly, fearing for their sheep and cattle, and that conflict can drive tourists and goodwill away rather than attract them.

toeflint.prompt: Summarize the points made in the lecture, being sure to explain how they cast doubt on the specific points made in the reading passage.
keyPoints: A few wolves may barely affect deer spread across a large area, as the deer relocate.
Forest and species recovery can take decades and depends more on other factors.
Wolves are rarely seen, and nearby farmers' opposition can outweigh any tourism gain.
